9.1.4.m: Four play for it: a Brahmin, a rājanya, a vaiśya, and a śūdra.

9.1.4.s: teṣām̐ yaḥ parājayate sa yajamānasya goṣu paṣṭhauhīm apisṛjati /
9.1.4.d: तेषाम्̐ यः पराजयते स यजमानस्य गोषु पष्ठौहीम् अपिसृजति /
9.1.4.m: Whichever of them loses, he releases that four-year-old cow among the cows of the sacrificer.

9.1.4.s: tataś catuḥśatam akṣān avohyāha \\ udbhinnam̐ rājñas \\ iti // diśo abhyabhūd ayam iti pañcākṣān yajamānāya prayachati /
9.1.4.d: ततश् चतुःशतम् अक्षान् अवोह्याह \\ उद्भिन्नम्̐ राज्ञस् \\ इति // दिशो अभ्यभूद् अयम् इति पञ्चाक्षान् यजमानाय प्रयछति /
9.1.4.m: Then, having set aside one hundred and four dice, he says, 'The king has won!' With 'This one has mastered the quarters', he hands five dice to the sacrificer.

9.1.4.s: kṣetraṃ brahmaṇe dadāti / varam̐ vṛṇīte /
9.1.4.d: क्षेत्रं ब्रह्मणे ददाति / वरम्̐ वृणीते /
9.1.4.m: He gives a field to the brahman priest; he chooses a boon.

9.1.4.s: maṅgalyānāmno hvayati suślokāḥ \ sumaṅgalāḥ \ satyarājānas \\ iti /
9.1.4.d: मङ्गल्यानाम्नो ह्वयति सुश्लोकाः \ सुमङ्गलाः \ सत्यराजानस् \\ इति /
9.1.4.m: He calls persons of auspicious names: 'O ones of fair renown, O ones of good auspices, O true kings!'

9.1.4.s: patnīloke pratihitasya mātaram upaspṛśya pratihitam anvārabhya prajāpate na tvad ity etayā gārhapatye nāmavyatiṣaṅgaṃ juhoti pālāśasaṃpātam //
9.1.4.d: पत्नीलोके प्रतिहितस्य मातरम् उपस्पृश्य प्रतिहितम् अन्वारभ्य प्रजापते न त्वद् इत्य् एतया गार्हपत्ये नामव्यतिषङ्गं जुहोति पालाशसंपातम् //
9.1.4.m: In the place of the wife, having touched the mother of the designated [substitute], having taken hold from behind of the designated [substitute], he offers the intertwined names into the gārhapatya fire with "O Prajāpati, no other than you...", accompanied by drops from a palāśa-leaf ladle.

9.1.4.s: asā amuṣya putro 'muṣyāsau putras \\ iti nāmanī vyatiṣajati //
9.1.4.d: असा अमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्यासौ पुत्रस् \\ इति नामनी व्यतिषजति //
9.1.4.m: He intertwines the two names: "So-and-so, the son of so-and-so; so-and-so, the son of so-and-so."

9.1.4.s: vayam̐ syāma patayo rayīṇām iti pratihitam̐ vācayati /
9.1.4.d: वयम्̐ स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् इति प्रतिहितम्̐ वाचयति /
9.1.4.m: He makes the designated [substitute] recite: "May we be masters of riches!"

9.1.4.s: mārutasya payasyāś ca samavādāyeḍām upahūya bhakṣayante /
9.1.4.d: मारुतस्य पयस्याश् च समवादायेडाम् उपहूय भक्षयन्ते /
9.1.4.m: Having cut off together [portions] of the [cake] to the Maruts and of the curd offering, having invoked the iḍā portion, they eat [it].

9.1.5.m: Beginning with the [cup] for Mahendra, [the procedure is] established up to the final bath.

9.1.5.s: vāsām̐sy abhiṣekapātrāṇi vārāhī ca prativeśam avabhṛtham̐ hareyuḥ /
9.1.5.d: वासाम्̐स्य् अभिषेकपात्राणि वाराही च प्रतिवेशम् अवभृथम्̐ हरेयुः /
9.1.5.m: They should take the garments, the vessels for the consecration, and the boar-skin [shoes] to a neighboring avabhṛtha.
He goes down to the avabhṛtha wearing gāgula-garments.

9.1.5.s: apāṃ naptre svāhā \\ ity avabhṛthe 'psu juhot \\ ūrjo naptre svāhā \\ iti darbhastambe dvitīyam agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā \\ iti gārhapatye /
9.1.5.d: अपां नप्त्रे स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अवभृथे ऽप्सु जुहोत् \\ ऊर्जो नप्त्रे स्वाहा \\ इति दर्भस्तम्बे द्वितीयम् अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा \\ इति गार्हपत्ये /
9.1.5.m: He makes an offering into the water with: 'To the Child of the Waters, svāhā!' at the avabhṛtha, a second into a clump of darbha grass with: 'To the Child of Vigour, svāhā!', [and a third] into the gārhapatya with: 'To Agni, master of the household, svāhā!'
The procedure is established up to the anūbandhyā cow.
The anūbandhyā is a barren cow that has calved; he causes her to step across with a four-footed [verse] having the word 'asūnīti'.
He apportions wild rice for the animal sacrificial cake.
He does not have his hair and beard shaved.
He does not undergo consecration; he hands over the staff.
He departs with the Sāvitra [offering]: [the portion] for the sacrificer in the gārhapatya, for the wife in the southern fire.

9.1.5.s: sam̐sṛpsu tadbhakṣau bhakṣayataḥ / sā vratāgnihotrayoḥ saṃtatiḥ /
9.1.5.d: सम्̐सृप्सु तद्भक्षौ भक्षयतः / सा व्रताग्निहोत्रयोः संततिः /
9.1.5.m: During the Saṃsṛp offerings they both consume their portions. That is the continuity of the vows and the agnihotra.
The ten Saṃsṛp offerings begin with the eight-potsherd cake to Savitṛ.

9.1.5.s: tāsām āhavanīyasthāne gārhapatyaṃ nidhāya prācīnam̐ sam̐sarpann anvaham̐ yajeta /
9.1.5.d: तासाम् आहवनीयस्थाने गार्हपत्यं निधाय प्राचीनम्̐ सम्̐सर्पन्न् अन्वहम्̐ यजेत /
9.1.5.m: Having placed the gārhapatya in the place of the āhavanīya for these, creeping eastward, he should sacrifice day after day.
Just as he would perform the Vaiṣṇava offering for the Daśapeya in the hall with eastward-pointing rafters,

9.1.5.s: daśapeyāya dīkṣate / dvādaśapuṇḍarīkāṃ mālām̐ yajamānaḥ pratimuñcate / sāpsu dīkṣā /
9.1.5.d: दशपेयाय दीक्षते / द्वादशपुण्डरीकां मालाम्̐ यजमानः प्रतिमुञ्चते / साप्सु दीक्षा /
9.1.5.m: he is consecrated for the Daśapeya. The sacrificer puts on a garland of twelve lotuses. That is the consecration in water.

9.1.5.s: sadyaḥ sarvaṃ kurvanti / kṛṣṇājinamekhalāviṣāṇāstanugrahaṃ kuryād anyaddīkṣitaṃ na prayachati /
9.1.5.d: सद्यः सर्वं कुर्वन्ति / कृष्णाजिनमेखलाविषाणास्तनुग्रहं कुर्याद् अन्यद्दीक्षितं न प्रयछति /
9.1.5.m: They perform everything in a single day. He should perform the retention of the body by means of the black antelope skin, the girdle, and the horn; he does not hand over anything else pertaining to a consecrated person.

9.1.5.s: prāyaṇīyasya haviṣkṛtā vācam̐ visṛjyābhyardhe rājānaṃ nivapati /
9.1.5.d: प्रायणीयस्य हविष्कृता वाचम्̐ विसृज्याभ्यर्धे राजानं निवपति /
9.1.5.m: Having released speech with the haviṣkṛt formula of the introductory offering, he apportions the King [Soma] aside.

9.1.5.s: prāyaṇīyam̐ sam̐sthāpya purastāt krītasya vatsatarān apākaroti svajā asi \\ itiprabhṛtibhiḥ /
9.1.5.d: प्रायणीयम्̐ सम्̐स्थाप्य पुरस्तात् क्रीतस्य वत्सतरान् अपाकरोति स्वजा असि \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिः /
9.1.5.m: Having concluded the introductory offering, he drives away the calves in front of the purchased [Soma] with the formulas beginning with: 'You are self-born.'
On the next day, there is the Daśapeya-Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara as the pṛṣṭha-sāman.

9.1.5.s: śataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ somān bhakṣayanti daśadaśaikaikaṃ camasam ā daśamān mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaś cānvākhyāya /
9.1.5.d: शतं ब्राह्मणाः सोमान् भक्षयन्ति दशदशैकैकं चमसम् आ दशमान् मातृतः पितृतश् चान्वाख्याय /
9.1.5.m: A hundred brāhmaṇas consume the Soma cups, ten to each single cup, after recounting [their ancestry] up to the tenth degree on both the mother's and father's sides.

9.1.5.s: na brāhmaṇanyaṅgo bhakṣayed dāsīputro nanv ācakṣīta kāmaṃ bhakṣayet /
9.1.5.d: न ब्राह्मणन्यङ्गो भक्षयेद् दासीपुत्रो नन्व् आचक्षीत कामं भक्षयेत् /
9.1.5.m: One who is deficient in brāhmaṇa status should not consume; [even] the son of a female slave, if he can recite [the lineage], may consume at will.

9.1.5.s: sahasratamīm atikālyāṃ rukmo hotur itiprabhṛti yathāmnātam apākaroti /
9.1.5.d: सहस्रतमीम् अतिकाल्यां रुक्मो होतुर् इतिप्रभृति यथाम्नातम् अपाकरोति /
9.1.5.m: He drives away the thousandth [cow] to be led past, and distributes the golden ornament of the hotṛ and so forth, as handed down.

9.1.5.s: ajaḥ subrahmaṇyasya vatsataryun netuḥ sāṇḍas trivatso grāvastuto dvādaśa paṣṭhauhīr garbhiṇīr brahmaṇaḥ /
9.1.5.d: अजः सुब्रह्मण्यस्य वत्सतर्युन् नेतुः साण्डस् त्रिवत्सो ग्रावस्तुतो द्वादश पष्ठौहीर् गर्भिणीर् ब्रह्मणः /
9.1.5.m: A goat is the subrahmaṇya's [gift], a heifer the unnetṛ's, an uncastrated three-year-old steer the grāvastut's, and twelve pregnant four-year-old heifers the brahman's.
He does not give to those who creep forward.

9.1.5.s: anūbandhyāyai sahasram atikālyā ṛtvigbhyaḥ somapebhyo dadāti /
9.1.5.d: अनूबन्ध्यायै सहस्रम् अतिकाल्या ऋत्विग्भ्यः सोमपेभ्यो ददाति /
9.1.5.m: Along with the thousandth [cow] led past for the anūbandhyā, he gives [cows] to the officiating priests who drink Soma.
He does not have his hair and beard shaved.
He departs with the Aveṣṭis of the quarters.
He apportions five [oblations], beginning with the eight-potsherd cake to Agni.

9.1.5.s: sāyaṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ purastāt prātaragnihotrāt prayugbhir yajata āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ saumyaś carur itiprabhṛtīni ṣaḍ dakṣiṇo rathavāhanavāho dakṣiṇā /
9.1.5.d: सायं पौर्णमास्यां पुरस्तात् प्रातरग्निहोत्रात् प्रयुग्भिर् यजत आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः सौम्यश् चरुर् इतिप्रभृतीनि षड् दक्षिणो रथवाहनवाहो दक्षिणा /
9.1.5.m: In the evening on the full-moon day, before the morning agnihotra, he sacrifices with the Prayuj offerings: six [oblations] beginning with the eight-potsherd cake to Agni and the caru to Soma; the sacrificial gift is the right draught-beast of the chariot.

9.1.5.s: śvobhūte paurṇamāsyeṣṭvottarāḥ prayuja upaiti sārasvataś caruḥ pauṣṇaś carur itiprabhṛtīni ṣaṭ savyo rathavāhanavāho dakṣiṇā /
9.1.5.d: श्वोभूते पौर्णमास्येष्ट्वोत्तराः प्रयुज उपैति सारस्वतश् चरुः पौष्णश् चरुर् इतिप्रभृतीनि षट् सव्यो रथवाहनवाहो दक्षिणा /
9.1.5.m: On the next day, having sacrificed with the full-moon sacrifice, he undertakes the subsequent Prayuj offerings: six [oblations] beginning with the caru to Sarasvatī and the caru to Pūṣan; the sacrificial gift is the left draught-beast of the chariot.

9.1.5.s: śvobhūte paśubandho māruto pṛśniḥ paṣṭhauhī garbhiṇī /
9.1.5.d: श्वोभूते पशुबन्धो मारुतो पृश्निः पष्ठौही गर्भिणी /
9.1.5.m: On the next day is an animal sacrifice to the Maruts: a spotted, pregnant four-year-old heifer.
On the next day is the subsequent [animal sacrifice] to the Ādityas: a pregnant, [hornless] female goat.

9.1.5.s: sāyam̐ somena pratipadya sam̐vatsaram agnihotram eva juhoty ā deśāt paśubandhād dvyahedvyahe vā /
9.1.5.d: सायम्̐ सोमेन प्रतिपद्य सम्̐वत्सरम् अग्निहोत्रम् एव जुहोत्य् आ देशात् पशुबन्धाद् द्व्यहेद्व्यहे वा /
9.1.5.m: Having commenced with the Soma sacrifice in the evening, he offers only the agnihotra for a year, up to the designated animal sacrifice, or [he sacrifices] every second day.

9.1.5.s: yo dhīvyavasitaḥ satyasitaḥ sātyadūtahavirbhir yajate savitre prasavitra itiprabhṛtīni trīṇi /
9.1.5.d: यो धीव्यवसितः सत्यसितः सात्यदूतहविर्भिर् यजते सवित्रे प्रसवित्र इतिप्रभृतीनि त्रीणि /
9.1.5.m: He who is firm in resolve and fixed in truth sacrifices with the oblations of the true messenger: three [oblations] beginning with [the one] to Savitṛ Prasavitṛ.

9.1.5.s: aśvaḥ śoṇakarṇo dakṣiṇā daṇḍa upānahau śuṣkadṛtiś ca /
9.1.5.d: अश्वः शोणकर्णो दक्षिणा दण्ड उपानहौ शुष्कदृतिश् च /
9.1.5.m: The sacrificial gift is a horse with red ears, a staff, a pair of sandals, and a dried skin bag.

9.1.5.s: tebhyaḥ pradāya prativeśāya rājñe prahinoti \\ abhyaṣikṣi rājābhūvam iti /
9.1.5.d: तेभ्यः प्रदाय प्रतिवेशाय राज्ञे प्रहिनोति \\ अभ्यषिक्षि राजाभूवम् इति /
9.1.5.m: Having given [these gifts] to them, he sends a messenger to a neighboring king, [announcing]: 'I have been consecrated, I have become king!'
On the full-moon day, he is consecrated for the Keśavapanīya.

9.1.5.s: amāvāsyāyām̐ yajanīye 'hany atirātraḥ kratur aṣoḍaśikaḥ sahasradakṣiṇaḥ /
9.1.5.d: अमावास्यायाम्̐ यजनीये ऽहन्य् अतिरात्रः क्रतुर् अषोडशिकः सहस्रदक्षिणः /
9.1.5.m: On the new-moon day, the day of sacrificing, there is an Atirātra rite with no sixteenth recitation, with a thousand [cows] as sacrificial gift.

9.1.5.s:
vapanakāla āsandyām āsīnaḥ
ye keśinaḥ prathame satram āsata \ yebhir idam̐ viśvaṃ bhuvanam ā virājati /
tasmā arcāma kṛṇavāma niṣkṛtim\ śaṃ no astu dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade //
iti nikhilaṃ keśaśmaśrū yajamāno vāpayate / prajñātam udavasānam /
9.1.5.d:
वपनकाल आसन्द्याम् आसीनः
ये केशिनः प्रथमे सत्रम् आसत \ येभिर् इदम्̐ विश्वं भुवनम् आ विराजति /
तस्मा अर्चाम कृणवाम निष्कृतिम्\ शं नो अस्तु द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे //
इति निखिलं केशश्मश्रू यजमानो वापयते / प्रज्ञातम् उदवसानम् /
9.1.5.m:
At the time of shaving, seated on a throne,

'Those long-haired ones who first sat at the sacrificial session, / by whom this entire universe shines bright,

to him let us offer worship and make amends; / may there be well-being for our two-footed, well-being for our four-footed [creatures],'

reciting this, the sacrificer has his hair and beard entirely shaved. The departure is well known.
Immediately after, he is consecrated with the dice for the ahīna sacrifice.

9.1.5.s: jyotir agniṣṭomaḥ pūrvo 'māvāsyāyām̐ yajanīye 'hany atirātraḥ / prajñātam udavasānam /
9.1.5.d: ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमः पूर्वो ऽमावास्यायाम्̐ यजनीये ऽहन्य् अतिरात्रः / प्रज्ञातम् उदवसानम् /
9.1.5.m: The first is the Jyotir-Agniṣṭoma; on the new-moon day, the day of sacrificing, there is an Atirātra. The departure is well known.
Immediately after, he is consecrated for the Kṣatradhṛti.
It is a Triṣṭoma-Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara as the pṛṣṭha-sāman. The departure is well known.

9.1.5.s: anantaram iṣṭibhir yajeta devikābhir devasuvām̐ havirbhir aiṣṭikyā sautrāmaṇyā vaiśvānaravāruṇyā traidhātavyayā traidhātavyayā /
9.1.5.d: अनन्तरम् इष्टिभिर् यजेत देविकाभिर् देवसुवाम्̐ हविर्भिर् ऐष्टिक्या सौत्रामण्या वैश्वानरवारुण्या त्रैधातव्यया त्रैधातव्यया /
9.1.5.m: Immediately after, he should sacrifice with the [following] iṣṭis: with the Devikā oblations, the Devasū oblations, the Sautrāmaṇī in iṣṭi form, the Vaiśvānarī-Vāruṇī, and the Traidhātavīyā, the Traidhātavīyā.

9.2.1.s: puṇyanāmni devayajane rājāśvamedhena yajeta sarvān kāmān avarurutsamāno 'muṃ ca lokam abhijigīṣan /
9.2.1.d: पुण्यनाम्नि देवयजने राजाश्वमेधेन यजेत सर्वान् कामान् अवरुरुत्समानो ऽमुं च लोकम् अभिजिगीषन् /
9.2.1.m: On a sacred-named sacrificial ground, a king should sacrifice with the Aśvamedha, desiring to secure all desires and wishing to conquer that world.

9.2.1.s: apadātīn ṛtvijaḥ samān āvahanti /
9.2.1.d: अपदातीन् ऋत्विजः समान् आवहन्ति /
9.2.1.m: They bring equal officiating priests who do not travel on foot.

9.2.1.s: phālgunyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ prājāpatyam ṛṣabhaṃ tūparam̐ sarvarūpam ālabheta /
9.2.1.d: फाल्गुन्यां पौर्णमास्यां प्राजापत्यम् ऋषभं तूपरम्̐ सर्वरूपम् आलभेत /
9.2.1.m: On the Phālguna full-moon day, he should seize a hornless, all-colored bull dedicated to Prajāpati.

9.2.1.s: hutāyām̐ vapāyāṃ cātvāle mārjayitvā sarvā diśo rathā abhidhāvanti /
9.2.1.d: हुतायाम्̐ वपायां चात्वाले मार्जयित्वा सर्वा दिशो रथा अभिधावन्ति /
9.2.1.m: When the omentum has been offered, having purified themselves at the cātvāla trench, chariots race out in all directions.

9.2.1.s: rājāśvamedhena yajeta tam anujānīteti /
9.2.1.d: राजाश्वमेधेन यजेत तम् अनुजानीतेति /
9.2.1.m: 'The king would sacrifice with the Aśvamedha; give him your consent!' [they proclaim].

9.2.1.s: sa siddhaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate /
9.2.1.d: स सिद्धः संतिष्ठते /
9.2.1.m: That [sacrifice] is established and concludes.

9.2.1.s: etam evālabheta sarvakāmaḥ /
9.2.1.d: एतम् एवालभेत सर्वकामः /
9.2.1.m: One who desires all things should seize this very [animal].

9.2.1.s: pūrvāṃ paurṇamāsīm upoṣyottarām upavaset /
9.2.1.d: पूर्वां पौर्णमासीम् उपोष्योत्तराम् उपवसेत् /
9.2.1.m: Having fasted on the first full-moon day, he should observe the Upavasatha on the second.

9.2.1.s: brahmaudanāyāstamayam anu vācam̐ yachanti /
9.2.1.d: ब्रह्मौदनायास्तमयम् अनु वाचम्̐ यछन्ति /
9.2.1.m: For the sake of the brahmaudana, they restrain their speech until sunset.

9.2.1.s: udite vaitasam idhmam upasamādhāya draṣṭre namas \\ upadraṣṭre namas \\ itiprabhṛtibhir ādityam upatiṣṭhate //
9.2.1.d: उदिते वैतसम् इध्मम् उपसमाधाय द्रष्ट्रे नमस् \\ उपद्रष्ट्रे नमस् \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् आदित्यम् उपतिष्ठते //
9.2.1.m: When [the sun] has risen, having placed reed sacrificial fuel [on the fire], he worships the sun with the formulas beginning with, 'Homage to the beholder, homage to the onlooker.'

9.2.1.s: hiraṇyagarbhas \\ iti dvādaśa pūrṇāhutīr juhoti /
9.2.1.d: हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ इति द्वादश पूर्णाहुतीर् जुहोति /
9.2.1.m: He offers twelve full oblations with the formulas beginning with, 'The Golden Embryo.'

9.2.1.s: catuṣkeṣv apsu dakṣiṇāgnau brahmaudanam̐ śrapayati rukmān abhito 'dhastād rājatam upariṣṭāt sauvarṇam /
9.2.1.d: चतुष्केष्व् अप्सु दक्षिणाग्नौ ब्रह्मौदनम्̐ श्रपयति रुक्मान् अभितो ऽधस्ताद् राजतम् उपरिष्टात् सौवर्णम् /
9.2.1.m: In four [measures of] water, he cooks the rice mess for the priests on the southern fire, with gold plates on both sides: a silver one below, a golden one above.

9.2.1.s: paścād gārhapatyasya madhyātkāriṇaḥ prāśnanti /
9.2.1.d: पश्चाद् गार्हपत्यस्य मध्यात्कारिणः प्राश्नन्ति /
9.2.1.m: Behind the gārhapatya fire, the principal officiating priests consume [it].

9.2.1.s: tebhyaḥ śatamānaṃ dadāti /
9.2.1.d: तेभ्यः शतमानं ददाति /
9.2.1.m: To them he gives a hundred-māna [weight of gold].

9.2.1.s: mauñjīṃ darbhamayīm̐ vā dvādaśāratniṃ trayodaśāratnim̐ vābhidhānīṃ brahmaudanena nyudya \\ imām agṛbhṇann iti raśanām ādatte //
9.2.1.d: मौञ्जीं दर्भमयीम्̐ वा द्वादशारत्निं त्रयोदशारत्निम्̐ वाभिधानीं ब्रह्मौदनेन न्युद्य \\ इमाम् अगृभ्णन्न् इति रशनाम् आदत्ते //
9.2.1.m: Having moistened a halter made of muñja grass or darbha grass, twelve cubits or thirteen cubits long, with the rice mess for the priests, he takes the halter with the formula, 'They have grasped this [halter of the cosmic order].'

9.2.1.s: brahmann aśvaṃ bhantsyāmi \\ iti brahmāṇam āmantrayate //
9.2.1.d: ब्रह्मन्न् अश्वं भन्त्स्यामि \\ इति ब्रह्माणम् आमन्त्रयते //
9.2.1.m: He addresses the brahman priest with the words, 'O brahman, I shall bind the horse.'

9.2.1.s: taṃ badhāna devebhyas \\ ity anujānāti //
9.2.1.d: तं बधान देवेभ्यस् \\ इत्य् अनुजानाति //
9.2.1.m: [The brahman priest] gives assent with the words, 'Bind him for the gods.'

9.2.1.s: abhidhā asi \\ iti trihāyaṇam aśvam abhinidadhāti kṛṣṇaṃ piśaṅgam aruṇapiśaṅgam̐ vā somapam̐ somapayoḥ putram /
9.2.1.d: अभिधा असि \\ इति त्रिहायणम् अश्वम् अभिनिदधाति कृष्णं पिशङ्गम् अरुणपिशङ्गम्̐ वा सोमपम्̐ सोमपयोः पुत्रम् /
9.2.1.m: With the formula, 'You are the binder,' he fastens [the halter] on a three-year-old horse that is black, yellowish-brown, or reddish-brown, that drinks soma, the son of parents who drink soma.

9.2.1.s: pitur anujāyāḥ putram agrato nayanti / śvānaṃ caturakṣam̐ saidhrakeṇa musalena paum̐ścaleyo 'nvaiti /
9.2.1.d: पितुर् अनुजायाः पुत्रम् अग्रतो नयन्ति / श्वानं चतुरक्षम्̐ सैध्रकेण मुसलेन पौम्̐श्चलेयो ऽन्वैति /
9.2.1.m: They lead the son of the father's younger sister in front; a son of a courtesan follows behind with a four-eyed dog [and] a pestle of saidhraka wood.

9.2.1.s: apo 'bhyavanīyāśvaṃ purastāt pratyaṅmukham avasthāpayati /
9.2.1.d: अपो ऽभ्यवनीयाश्वं पुरस्तात् प्रत्यङ्मुखम् अवस्थापयति /
9.2.1.m: Having led the horse down into the water, he makes him stand in the east facing west.

9.2.1.s: sarvais taiḥ sārdhaṃ catvāro 'dhvaryavaḥ //
9.2.1.d: सर्वैस् तैः सार्धं चत्वारो ऽध्वर्यवः //
9.2.1.m: Together with all of them, the four adhvaryu priests [act].

9.2.1.s: prajāpataye tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmi \\ itiprabhṛtibhir ekaikāt prokṣati sarvebhyas tvā devebhyas \\ iti sarve sarvataḥ /
9.2.1.d: प्रजापतये त्वा जुष्टं प्रोक्षामि \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् एकैकात् प्रोक्षति सर्वेभ्यस् त्वा देवेभ्यस् \\ इति सर्वे सर्वतः /
9.2.1.m: Each one sprinkles [the horse] individually with the formulas beginning with, 'I sprinkle you agreeable to Prajāpati'; all of them sprinkle [him] from all sides with, 'To all the gods, you.'

9.2.1.s: saidhrakeṇa musalena paum̐ścaleyaḥ śvānam̐ hanti //
9.2.1.d: सैध्रकेण मुसलेन पौम्̐श्चलेयः श्वानम्̐ हन्ति //
9.2.1.m: The son of the courtesan kills the dog with the pestle of saidhraka wood.

9.2.1.s: yo arvantaṃ jighām̐sati \\ iti hanyamāne japati yajamānaḥ /
9.2.1.d: यो अर्वन्तं जिघाम्̐सति \\ इति हन्यमाने जपति यजमानः /
9.2.1.m: While it is being killed, the sacrificer mutters, 'Whoever seeks to kill the courser.'

9.2.1.s: dakṣiṇaṃ padaṃ pūrvam upodyamya paro martaḥ paraḥ śvā \\ ity adhastāc chvānaṃ dakṣiṇāpaḥ plāvayati /
9.2.1.d: दक्षिणं पदं पूर्वम् उपोद्यम्य परो मर्तः परः श्वा \\ इत्य् अधस्ताच् छ्वानं दक्षिणापः प्लावयति /
9.2.1.m: Having first lifted the [horse's] right foot, he floats the dog beneath [it] towards the south with the formula, 'Away is the mortal, away the dog.'

9.2.1.s: utkrāmantam aśvam aiṣīkenodūhena vetasaśākhayābhyudūhanti //
9.2.1.d: उत्क्रामन्तम् अश्वम् ऐषीकेनोदूहेन वेतसशाखयाभ्युदूहन्ति //
9.2.1.m: As the horse steps out, they brush him up with a whisk of reed grass [and] with a branch of rattan.

9.2.1.s: agnaye svāhā \ somāya svāhā \\ ity anuvākena kṣarantam anumantrayate //
9.2.1.d: अग्नये स्वाहा \ सोमाय स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन क्षरन्तम् अनुमन्त्रयते //
9.2.1.m: With the section beginning with, 'To Agni svāhā! To Soma svāhā!', he accompanies with a mantra [the horse] as it steps forth.

9.2.1.s: idam̐ viṣṇuḥ \ pra tad viṣṇur \ divo viṣṇa iti triṣu padeṣu juhoti prodake //
9.2.1.d: इदम्̐ विष्णुः \ प्र तद् विष्णुर् \ दिवो विष्ण इति त्रिषु पदेषु जुहोति प्रोदके //
9.2.1.m: With the formulas, 'Here Viṣṇu [strode],' 'Forth that Viṣṇu,' and 'From the sky, Viṣṇu,' he offers [libations] on the three footprints in the water.

9.2.1.s: vibhūr mātrā prabhūḥ pitrā \\ ity aśvam abhimantrayate //
9.2.1.d: विभूर् मात्रा प्रभूः पित्रा \\ इत्य् अश्वम् अभिमन्त्रयते //
9.2.1.m: With the formula, 'Mighty by mother, prevailing by father,' he consecrates the horse.

9.2.1.s: ādityānāṃ patvānvihi \\ ity utsṛjati /
9.2.1.d: आदित्यानां पत्वान्विहि \\ इत्य् उत्सृजति /
9.2.1.m: With the formula, 'Follow the flight of the Ādityas,' he sets [the horse] free.

9.2.1.s: śatāya kavacināṃ talpyebhyo rājaputrebhyas \\ devā āśāpālās \\ ity aśvaṃ paridadāti /
9.2.1.d: शताय कवचिनां तल्प्येभ्यो राजपुत्रेभ्यस् \\ देवा आशापालास् \\ इत्य् अश्वं परिददाति /
9.2.1.m: With the formula, 'Gods who protect the quarters,' he entrusts the horse to a hundred princes of royal beds, clad in armor.

9.2.1.s: catuḥśatāḥ pālayanty anivartayantaḥ /
9.2.1.d: चतुःशताः पालयन्त्य् अनिवर्तयन्तः /
9.2.1.m: Four hundred [guards] protect him without turning him back.

9.2.2.m: He proceeds with the Sāvitra offerings in a whisper.
In the forenoon, he should apportion [an oblation] on eight potsherds to Savitṛ.

9.2.2.s: hiṃkārāya svāhā \\ itiprabhṛtibhir ekatra pañcāśatam āhutīr juhoti /
9.2.2.d: हिंकाराय स्वाहा \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् एकत्र पञ्चाशतम् आहुतीर् जुहोति /
9.2.2.m: With the formulas beginning with, 'To the sound hiṃ svāhā!', he offers fifty-one oblations in one place.

9.2.2.s: savitre prasavitra ekādaśakapālaṃ madhyaṃdine / savitre prasavitre dvādaśakapālam aparāhṇe //
9.2.2.d: सवित्रे प्रसवित्र एकादशकपालं मध्यंदिने / सवित्रे प्रसवित्रे द्वादशकपालम् अपराह्णे //
9.2.2.m: At midday, [an oblation] on eleven potsherds to Savitṛ the Impeller; in the afternoon, [an oblation] on twelve potsherds to Savitṛ the Impeller.

9.2.2.s: iha dhṛtir \ iha svadhṛtir itiprabhṛtibhiḥ prāk sviṣṭakṛtaś catasra āhutīr juhoti /
9.2.2.d: इह धृतिर् \ इह स्वधृतिर् इतिप्रभृतिभिः प्राक् स्विष्टकृतश् चतस्र आहुतीर् जुहोति /
9.2.2.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers four oblations with the formulas beginning with, 'Here is steadfastness, here is firm steadfastness.'
For a year he should sacrifice with the seasonal offerings and make the oblations.

9.2.2.s: vīṇāgāthināv upagāyetām ity ayajathās \\ ity apacathās \\ ity adadās \\ iti tisṛbhir divā brāhmaṇas \\ ity ayudhyathās \\ iti kalyāṇam akuruthās \\ ity amum̐ saṃgrāmam ajayathās \\ iti tisṛbhir naktam̐ rājanya iti /
9.2.2.d: वीणागाथिनाव् उपगायेताम् इत्य् अयजथास् \\ इत्य् अपचथास् \\ इत्य् अददास् \\ इति तिसृभिर् दिवा ब्राह्मणस् \\ इत्य् अयुध्यथास् \\ इति कल्याणम् अकुरुथास् \\ इत्य् अमुम्̐ संग्रामम् अजयथास् \\ इति तिसृभिर् नक्तम्̐ राजन्य इति /
9.2.2.m: Two lute-players should sing along: a brahmin by day with the three [verses], 'Thus did you sacrifice,' 'Thus did you cook,' 'Thus did you give,' [and] a noble by night with the three [verses], 'Thus did you fight,' 'Thus did you do good,' 'Thus did you conquer that battle.'

9.2.2.s: saṃnipāte nityāpūrvānāśācetaśaṃketāśvākhare nirvaped āśvinībhir dhānā mṛgākhare yadi nāgachet /
9.2.2.d: संनिपाते नित्यापूर्वानाशाचेतशंकेताश्वाखरे निर्वपेद् आश्विनीभिर् धाना मृगाखरे यदि नागछेत् /
9.2.2.m: In case of a clash, one should apportion regular unseen offerings [and] roasted grains at the horse's resting place with the Āśvina verses, or at a deer's resting place if he does not return.
A sacrifice is also handed down in tradition in the case of mating with a mare.
After a year, he performs the Ṣahamati sacrifice.
At that [rite], they prepare the fire-pot up to the lid.

9.2.2.s: samāpte vīṇāgāthibhyām̐ śate dadāty anasi yukte cāśvarathau /
9.2.2.d: समाप्ते वीणागाथिभ्याम्̐ शते ददात्य् अनसि युक्ते चाश्वरथौ /
9.2.2.m: When it is concluded, he gives a hundred [cows] to the two lute-players, and a cart harnessed with two horses.
Having confined the horse in an enclosure, they tame him.
On the seventh [day] is the animal sacrifice; on the eighth is the Traidhātavī initiation offering.
The ritual is established up to the recited yajus formulas.

9.2.2.s: kāya svāhā \ kasmai svāhā \\ itiprabhṛtīni trīṇi vaiśvadevyāny anvaham̐ saptamyāṃ pañcādhvarakāṇi hutvā ṣaḍ āgnikāni juhoty uttamāni ca vaiśvadevyāni /
9.2.2.d: काय स्वाहा \ कस्मै स्वाहा \\ इतिप्रभृतीनि त्रीणि वैश्वदेव्यान्य् अन्वहम्̐ सप्तम्यां पञ्चाध्वरकाणि हुत्वा षड् आग्निकानि जुहोत्य् उत्तमानि च वैश्वदेव्यानि /
9.2.2.m: On the seventh day, having daily offered three Vaiśvadeva formulas beginning with, 'To Ka svāhā! To Kasmai svāhā!', [and] five offerings for the rites, he offers six fire offerings and the final Vaiśvadeva formulas.
From the full oblation onward, the ritual is established up to the upasad days.

9.2.2.s: ā brahman brāhmaṇas \\ iti brahmā jātam ukhyam upatiṣṭhate /
9.2.2.d: आ ब्रह्मन् ब्राह्मणस् \\ इति ब्रह्मा जातम् उख्यम् उपतिष्ठते /
9.2.2.m: With the formula, 'Into the brahman, the brahmin,' the brahman priest worships the fire produced in the pot.
The initiation lasts a year; there are twelve upasad days.
The altar is three times larger, likewise the fire-altar, but not the high altar.
The two soma-cart sheds are chariot-stands.

9.2.2.s: yūpān ekavim̐śatim̐ saṃminoti / naicudāravo 'gniṣṭha ekavim̐śatyaratniḥ pautudāravāv upasthāvānau ṣaṭ khādirāḥ ṣaṭ pālāśāḥ ṣaḍ bailvās trayo 'nye trayo 'nye / madhyame vāhani vim̐śatim̐ saṃminoti /
9.2.2.d: यूपान् एकविम्̐शतिम्̐ संमिनोति / नैचुदारवो ऽग्निष्ठ एकविम्̐शत्यरत्निः पौतुदारवाव् उपस्थावानौ षट् खादिराः षट् पालाशाः षड् बैल्वास् त्रयो ऽन्ये त्रयो ऽन्ये / मध्यमे वाहनि विम्̐शतिम्̐ संमिनोति /
9.2.2.m: He sets up twenty-one sacrificial posts: the one facing the fire is made of pūtu-tree wood, twenty-one cubits long; the two flanking posts are made of pūtudāru wood; six are of khadira wood, six of palāśa wood, six of bilva wood, three of another kind, [and] three of yet another kind; or on the middle day he sets up twenty.

9.2.2.s: yathākālaṃ digbhyo vasatīvarīr gṛhītvā samānīya sādayaty evam uttarābhyām ukthyātirātrābhyām /
9.2.2.d: यथाकालं दिग्भ्यो वसतीवरीर् गृहीत्वा समानीय सादयत्य् एवम् उत्तराभ्याम् उक्थ्यातिरात्राभ्याम् /
9.2.2.m: Having collected the Vasatīvarī waters from the directions at the proper time, bringing them together, he places them; in the same way for the subsequent Ukthya and Atirātra days.
Daily he draws the additional Pṛṣṭhya cups.
On the middle [day], he should execute the Pṛṣṭhaśilpa.
On the next day, there is a Catuṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara as its pṛṣṭha stotra.
It concludes in the established manner ending with the offerings to the wives of the gods.
Sitting on low couches, both make offerings with two offering ladles at sunset.

9.2.2.s: saktūn dhānā masūsyāni karambhām̐l lājān pṛthukān priyaṅgutaṇḍulān sam̐sṛjyānnena juhoti \\ agnaye svāhā \ somāya svāhā \\ itiprabhṛtibhir aikaśatāt //
9.2.2.d: सक्तून् धाना मसूस्यानि करम्भाम्̐ल् लाजान् पृथुकान् प्रियङ्गुतण्डुलान् सम्̐सृज्यान्नेन जुहोति \\ अग्नये स्वाहा \ सोमाय स्वाहा \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् ऐकशतात् //
9.2.2.m: Having mixed barley groats, roasted grains, lentils, porridge, parched rice, flattened grains, and panic seeds, he offers with food, with formulas beginning with, 'To Agni svāhā! To Soma svāhā!', up to one hundred and one.

9.2.2.s: ekasmai svāhā \ dvābhyām̐ svāhā \\ ity etenābhyāvartayan sarvarātraṃ juhoti yugbhir annam ayugbhir ājyam \\ vyuṣṭyai svāhā \\ iti vyuṣṭāyām \\ svargāya svāhā \\ ity abhudite /
9.2.2.d: एकस्मै स्वाहा \ द्वाभ्याम्̐ स्वाहा \\ इत्य् एतेनाभ्यावर्तयन् सर्वरात्रं जुहोति युग्भिर् अन्नम् अयुग्भिर् आज्यम् \\ व्युष्ट्यै स्वाहा \\ इति व्युष्टायाम् \\ स्वर्गाय स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अभुदिते /
9.2.2.m: Repeating with the formulas, 'To one svāhā! To two svāhā!', he makes offerings throughout the whole night—food with the even ones, clarified butter with the odd ones; with, 'To dawn svāhā!', when dawn breaks; with, 'To heaven svāhā!', at sunrise.

9.2.3.d: एकविम्̐श उक्थ्यो मध्यमाहः /
9.2.3.m: The middle day is a twenty-one-fold Ukthya.

9.2.3.d: सिद्धम् आ पात्रप्रयोजनात् /
9.2.3.m: The procedure is established up to the employ of the vessels.

9.2.3.s: antaryāmapātraṃ prayujya mahimnoḥ pātre prayunakti sauvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇam̐ rājatam uttaram /
9.2.3.d: अन्तर्यामपात्रं प्रयुज्य महिम्नोः पात्रे प्रयुनक्ति सौवर्णं दक्षिणम्̐ राजतम् उत्तरम् /
9.2.3.m: Having employed the Antaryāma cup, he employs the two Mahiman cups: the golden one on the south, the silver one on the north.

9.2.3.d: सिद्धम् आ ग्रहणात् /

9.2.3.s: antaryāmaṃ gṛhītvā mahimānau gṛhṇīte hiraṇyagarbhas \\ yaḥ prāṇatas \\ iti grahaṇasādane /
9.2.3.d: अन्तर्यामं गृहीत्वा महिमानौ गृह्णीते हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ यः प्राणतस् \\ इति ग्रहणसादने /
9.2.3.m: Having drawn the Antaryāma cup, he draws the two Mahiman cups; the drawing and placing [are accompanied] by the verses, 'The Golden Embryo' [and] 'He who breathes.'

9.2.3.d: सिद्धम् आ बहिष्पवमानात् /
9.2.3.m: The ritual is established up to the out-of-doors laud.

9.2.3.s:
jyotir yajñasya pavate madhu priyam\ pitā devānāṃ janitā vibhāvasuḥ /
dadhāti ratnam̐ svadhayor apīcyam\ maditamo matsara indriyo rasaḥ //
ity aśvasya grīvāsu niṣkaṃ pratimuñcati //
9.2.3.d:
ज्योतिर् यज्ञस्य पवते मधु प्रियम्\ पिता देवानां जनिता विभावसुः /
दधाति रत्नम्̐ स्वधयोर् अपीच्यम्\ मदितमो मत्सर इन्द्रियो रसः //
इत्य् अश्वस्य ग्रीवासु निष्कं प्रतिमुञ्चति //
9.2.3.m:
'The light of the sacrifice is purified, the sweet soma, dear, / the father of the gods, the progenitor, possessing radiant wealth.'

"He sets the treasure in the secret place of the two worlds, / Most exhilarating, intoxicating, full of virile energy, the sap."

With this [verse] he fastens a gold ornament around the neck of the horse.

9.2.3.s: śyeno 'si gāyatraṃ chandaḥ \ suparṇo 'si triṣṭupchandaḥ \ sakhāsi gāyatraṃ chandas \\ ity aśvasya pucham ārabhya pavamānam̐ sarpanti /
9.2.3.d: श्येनो ऽसि गायत्रं छन्दः \ सुपर्णो ऽसि त्रिष्टुप्छन्दः \ सखासि गायत्रं छन्दस् \\ इत्य् अश्वस्य पुछम् आरभ्य पवमानम्̐ सर्पन्ति /
9.2.3.m: With: "You are a falcon, the gāyatrī metre; you are a bird of good wings, the triṣṭubh metre; you are a companion, the gāyatrī metre," they glide to the pavamāna chant, holding on to the tail of the horse.

9.2.3.s: uttarataḥ śatena tvā pravṛṇajmi \\ ity udgātāram āha tasyāpavaram ṛtvijo 'pavṛtāḥ /
9.2.3.d: उत्तरतः शतेन त्वा प्रवृणज्मि \\ इत्य् उद्गातारम् आह तस्यापवरम् ऋत्विजो ऽपवृताः /
9.2.3.m: "To the north, with a hundred I choose you," he says to the udgātṛ. At his choice, the officiating priests are chosen.

9.2.3.d: शतम् उद्गात्रे ददाति /
आस्तावान्ते वडवाम् अपसाध्याश्वम्̐ संक्रमयन्ति /
9.2.3.m: At the edge of the āstāva, having curbed a mare, they make the horse approach.

9.2.3.s: uttaratas \\ niṣkeṇa tvā śatapareṇopahvayāmas \\ imāṃ devatām udgāya \\ ity udgātāram āha tasyopahvānam ṛtvija imāṃ devatām upahūtāḥ /
9.2.3.d: उत्तरतस् \\ निष्केण त्वा शतपरेणोपह्वयामस् \\ इमां देवताम् उद्गाय \\ इत्य् उद्गातारम् आह तस्योपह्वानम् ऋत्विज इमां देवताम् उपहूताः /
9.2.3.m: To the north, [saying]: "With a gold ornament followed by a hundred we summon you; chant the udgītha for this deity," he speaks to the udgātṛ. At his summoning, the officiating priests are summoned for this deity.

9.2.3.d: शतं निष्कं चोद्गात्रे ददाति /
9.2.3.m: And he gives a hundred and a gold ornament to the udgātṛ.

9.2.3.d: उभयं कुर्वन्त्य् उद्गीथम् अश्वसंक्रन्दनं च /
9.2.3.m: They perform both: the chanting of the udgītha and the neighing of the horse.

9.2.3.d: समाप्ते शतमानम् उद्गातृभ्यः प्रयछति /
9.2.3.m: When it is finished, he presents a śatamāna [weight of gold] to the udgātṛs.

9.2.3.d: सिद्धम् ओपाकरणात् /

9.2.3.s: dvayānaikādaśinān upākaroti plakṣaśākhayetarān aśve paryaṅgyān avachādayanto yāmam indrāya svapasyāya vehad vaiṣṇavo vāmana iti yūpabhājo babhrur aruṇababhrur itiprabhṛtīn viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ pṛṣata ity antān /
9.2.3.d: द्वयानैकादशिनान् उपाकरोति प्लक्षशाखयेतरान् अश्वे पर्यङ्ग्यान् अवछादयन्तो यामम् इन्द्राय स्वपस्याय वेहद् वैष्णवो वामन इति यूपभाजो बभ्रुर् अरुणबभ्रुर् इतिप्रभृतीन् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पृषत इत्य् अन्तान् /
9.2.3.m: He brings up two sets of eleven [victims]; with a branch of the plakṣa tree the other [wild animals]; while they cover the horse with the victims tied around its limbs: "To Yama, to Indra, for good work... a barren cow... to Viṣṇu a dwarf"—these are the sharers of the sacrificial post; "A brown one, a reddish-brown one," etc., ending with "spotted ones to the Viśve Devas."

9.2.3.s: bahuśabde trīn pratīyāt tryavayo gāyatryai \\ ity adhyardhahāyanān pañcāvayas triṣṭubhe pañcāvarān dityavāho jagatyai dvihāyanām̐s trivatsā anuṣṭubhe trihāyanām̐s turyavāha uṣṇihe caturhāyanān paṣṭhavāho virāje \\ iti paṣṭhauhaḥ //
9.2.3.d: बहुशब्दे त्रीन् प्रतीयात् त्र्यवयो गायत्र्यै \\ इत्य् अध्यर्धहायनान् पञ्चावयस् त्रिष्टुभे पञ्चावरान् दित्यवाहो जगत्यै द्विहायनाम्̐स् त्रिवत्सा अनुष्टुभे त्रिहायनाम्̐स् तुर्यवाह उष्णिहे चतुर्हायनान् पष्ठवाहो विराजे \\ इति पष्ठौहः //
9.2.3.m: Where a plural word is used, one should understand three. "Three-year-olds to the gāyatrī"—[meaning] one-and-a-half-year-old [animals]; "five-year-olds to the triṣṭubh"—at least five; "two-year-olds (dityavāh) to the jagatī"—two-year-old [animals]; "three-year-olds (trivatsa) to the anuṣṭubh"—three-year-old [animals]; "four-year-olds (turyavāh) to the uṣṇih"—four-year-old [animals]; "six-year-olds (paṣṭhavāh) to the virāj"—a six-year-old ox (paṣṭhauh).

9.2.3.s: yuñjanti bradhnam ity aruṇapiśaṅgam̐ yujyamānam anumantrayate yuñjanty asya kāmyā \\ ity uttarau ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave \\ iti dhvajam \\ jīmūtasyeva \\ iti saṃnaddhakavacaṃ dhatte ... tīṣudhim̐ rathe tiṣṭhan nayati iti sārathiṃ tīvrān ghoṣān kṛṇvate \\ ity aśvān vanaspate vīḍvaṅgas \\ iti tisṛbhī ratham̐ svādupam̐sadas \\ iti tisṛbhir janayataḥ suparṇam̐ vaste \\ itīṣum ahir iva bhogair iti talam ājaṅghanti \\ ity aśvājanīm upaśvāsaya \\ iti dvābhyāṃ dundubhim //
9.2.3.d: युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नम् इत्य् अरुणपिशङ्गम्̐ युज्यमानम् अनुमन्त्रयते युञ्जन्त्य् अस्य काम्या \\ इत्य् उत्तरौ केतुं कृण्वन्न् अकेतवे \\ इति ध्वजम् \\ जीमूतस्येव \\ इति संनद्धकवचं धत्ते ... तीषुधिम्̐ रथे तिष्ठन् नयति इति सारथिं तीव्रान् घोषान् कृण्वते \\ इत्य् अश्वान् वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गस् \\ इति तिसृभी रथम्̐ स्वादुपम्̐सदस् \\ इति तिसृभिर् जनयतः सुपर्णम्̐ वस्ते \\ इतीषुम् अहिर् इव भोगैर् इति तलम् आजङ्घन्ति \\ इत्य् अश्वाजनीम् उपश्वासय \\ इति द्वाभ्यां दुन्दुभिम् //
9.2.3.m: With "They yoke the tawny steed..." he accompanies with a mantra the reddish-tawny one as it is being yoked; with "They yoke his two dear..." the two following ones; with "Making a sign for him who has no sign..." the banner; with "Like a cloud..." he puts on the armored one [...]; [with "..."] the quiver; with "Standing in the chariot he directs..." the charioteer; with "They make loud noises..." the horses; with "O lord of the forest, strong-limbed..." with three [verses], the chariot; with "Pleasant to sit upon..." with three [verses], the two produce [...]; with "He wears a good feather..." the arrow; with "Like a serpent with its coils..." the arm-guard; with "They strike..." the whip; with "Make sound..." with two [verses], the war-drum.

9.2.3.d: आमूर् अज \\ इति जपति /
प्राग् अभिप्रयाय प्रदक्षिणम् आवर्तयति /
9.2.3.m: Having driven forward towards the east, he turns around clockwise.

9.2.3.s: prayuktānām aruṇapiśaṅgam apo 'bhyavanīya yad vāto 'po aganīgann iti pratyānayati yathopākṛtam avasthitam /
9.2.3.d: प्रयुक्तानाम् अरुणपिशङ्गम् अपो ऽभ्यवनीय यद् वातो ऽपो अगनीगन्न् इति प्रत्यानयति यथोपाकृतम् अवस्थितम् /
9.2.3.m: Having led the reddish-tawny one among the yoked ones down to the water, he brings it back with: "Since the wind has reached the water...", standing as it was when brought forward.

9.2.3.s: abhyañjanti vasavas tvāñjantu \\ iti kāsāmbavena mahiṣī mukhādadhyā bāhvas \\ rudrās tvāñjantu \\ iti gaulgulavena vāvātā nabher ādityās tvāñjantu \\ iti maustakṛtena parivṛktyā puchāt /
9.2.3.d: अभ्यञ्जन्ति वसवस् त्वाञ्जन्तु \\ इति कासाम्बवेन महिषी मुखादध्या बाह्वस् \\ रुद्रास् त्वाञ्जन्तु \\ इति गौल्गुलवेन वावाता नभेर् आदित्यास् त्वाञ्जन्तु \\ इति मौस्तकृतेन परिवृक्त्या पुछात् /
9.2.3.m: They anoint it: the chief queen (mahiṣī) anoints it from the mouth down to the forelegs with ointment of kāsāmba with: "May the Vasus anoint you"; the favorite wife (vāvātā) from the navel with bdellium ointment with: "May the Rudras anoint you"; the discarded wife (parivṛktī) from the tail with nut-grass ointment with: "May the Ādityas anoint you."

9.2.3.s: trisāhasrān kācām̐l lomasv āvayanti bhūr iti mahiṣī sauvarṇān bhuvas \\ iti vāvātā rājatān svar iti parivṛktī śaṅkhamayān //
9.2.3.d: त्रिसाहस्रान् काचाम्̐ल् लोमस्व् आवयन्ति भूर् इति महिषी सौवर्णान् भुवस् \\ इति वावाता राजतान् स्वर् इति परिवृक्ती शङ्खमयान् //
9.2.3.m: They weave three thousand glass beads into the hair: the chief queen weaves golden ones with "Bhūḥ"; the favorite wife silver ones with "Bhuvaḥ"; the discarded wife ones made of conch shell with "Svaḥ".

9.2.3.d: लाजी शाची \\ इत्य् अन्नहोमशेषं पत्न्यो ऽश्वायोपकिरन्ति /
9.2.3.m: With: "Lājī śācī..." the wives scatter the remainder of the food oblation for the horse.

9.2.3.d: यत्राद्यात् तद् इष्टके प्रकिरेत् /
9.2.3.m: Where it would eat, there he should scatter it on a brick.

9.2.3.d: आज्यम्̐ होमशेषम् अभिषेकाय निदधाति /
9.2.3.m: He sets aside the clarified butter that is the remainder of the oblation for the consecration.

9.2.3.s: hotā brahmā cānvagniṣṭham abhito 'nyo'nyaṃ pṛchataḥ kaḥ svid ekākī carati \ sūrya ekākī carati \\ iti praśnaprativacanāt /
9.2.3.d: होता ब्रह्मा चान्वग्निष्ठम् अभितो ऽन्योऽन्यं पृछतः कः स्विद् एकाकी चरति \ सूर्य एकाकी चरति \\ इति प्रश्नप्रतिवचनात् /
9.2.3.m: The hotṛ and the brahman priest ask each other on both sides of the central sacrificial post: "Who, indeed, roams alone?"—"The sun roams alone," following the questions and answers.

9.2.4.s: siddham ā niyojanāt //
9.2.4.d: सिद्धम् आ नियोजनात् //

9.2.4.s: yuñjanti bradhnam ity aruṇapiśaṅgam agniṣṭhe niyunakti tūparagomṛgau cāśvam abhito daśa paryaṅgyān avachādayanto yāmam indrāya svapasyāya vehad vaiṣṇavo vāmana iti yūpabhājo babhrur aruṇababhrur itiprabhṛtīn /
9.2.4.d: युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नम् इत्य् अरुणपिशङ्गम् अग्निष्ठे नियुनक्ति तूपरगोमृगौ चाश्वम् अभितो दश पर्यङ्ग्यान् अवछादयन्तो यामम् इन्द्राय स्वपस्याय वेहद् वैष्णवो वामन इति यूपभाजो बभ्रुर् अरुणबभ्रुर् इतिप्रभृतीन् /
9.2.4.m: With "They yoke the tawny steed..." he binds the reddish-tawny horse to the central sacrificial post; and on both sides of the horse a hornless goat and a wild ox; the ten victims tied around the limbs; while they cover [it]: "To Yama, to Indra, for good work... a barren cow... to Viṣṇu a dwarf"—these belong to the sacrificial posts, "A brown one, a reddish-brown one," and so forth.

9.2.4.s: vasantāya kapiñjalān itiprabhṛtaya āraṇyās teṣāṃ daśa pañcadaśina ekādaśa daśinaḥ /
9.2.4.d: वसन्ताय कपिञ्जलान् इतिप्रभृतय आरण्यास् तेषां दश पञ्चदशिन एकादश दशिनः /
9.2.4.m: Those beginning with "Francolin partridges for spring..." are the wild animals; of them, there are ten sets of fifteen and eleven sets of ten.

9.2.4.s: tān yūpāntareṣu trayodaśatrayodaśa vyatyāsaṃ / nāṅgiṣu pluṣimaśakān karaṇḍeṣu sarpān piñjareṣu mṛgavyāghrasim̐hān kumbheṣu makaramatsyamaṇḍūkāñjāleṣu pakṣiṇaḥ kārāsu hastinaḥ nauṣu caudakāni yathārtham itarān /
9.2.4.d: तान् यूपान्तरेषु त्रयोदशत्रयोदश व्यत्यासं / नाङ्गिषु प्लुषिमशकान् करण्डेषु सर्पान् पिञ्जरेषु मृगव्याघ्रसिम्̐हान् कुम्भेषु मकरमत्स्यमण्डूकाञ्जालेषु पक्षिणः कारासु हस्तिनः नौषु चौदकानि यथार्थम् इतरान् /
9.2.4.m: He places them between the sacrificial posts, thirteen by thirteen alternately: the fleas and mosquitoes in vessels; the snakes in hampers; the wild beasts, tigers, and lions in cages; the sea monsters, fish, and frogs in jars; the birds in nets; the elephants in enclosures; and the aquatic animals in boats; the others according to their suitability.

9.2.4.s: siddham ā paryagnikaraṇāt /
9.2.4.d: सिद्धम् आ पर्यग्निकरणात् /
9.2.4.m: [The procedure] is established up to the carrying of fire around [the victims] (paryagnikaraṇa).

9.2.4.s: paryagnikṛtān utsṛjanti puruṣānye ca grāmyāṇām utsarjanadharmāṇaḥ /
9.2.4.d: पर्यग्निकृतान् उत्सृजन्ति पुरुषान्ये च ग्राम्याणाम् उत्सर्जनधर्माणः /
9.2.4.m: After fire has been carried around them, they release the wild animals and whichever domestic animals have the rule of being released.

9.2.4.s: siddham ā prakramaṇāt /
9.2.4.d: सिद्धम् आ प्रक्रमणात् /

9.2.4.s: pauṣṇam ajam aśvasyāgrato nayanti /
9.2.4.d: पौष्णम् अजम् अश्वस्याग्रतो नयन्ति /
9.2.4.m: They lead the goat sacred to Pūṣan in front of the horse.

9.2.4.s: avasthitāyāśvāya darbham upāsyati vāso 'dhīvāso hiraṇyakaśipūni ca /
9.2.4.d: अवस्थितायाश्वाय दर्भम् उपास्यति वासो ऽधीवासो हिरण्यकशिपूनि च /
9.2.4.m: For the horse that has been brought to a standstill, he throws down darbha grass, a cloth, an upper garment, and gold cushions.

9.2.4.s: galāpraveṣṭanena prājāpatyān saṃjñapayanti śāmūlenāśvam //
9.2.4.d: गलाप्रवेष्टनेन प्राजापत्यान् संज्ञपयन्ति शामूलेनाश्वम् //
9.2.4.m: They suffocate the victims sacred to Prajāpati by encircling the neck, and the horse with a garment of wool (śāmūla).

9.2.4.s: prāṇāya svāhā \\ apānāya svāhā \ vyānāya svāhā \\ iti saṃjñapyamāne tisra āhutīr juhoti //
9.2.4.d: प्राणाय स्वाहा \\ अपानाय स्वाहा \ व्यानाय स्वाहा \\ इति संज्ञप्यमाने तिस्र आहुतीर् जुहोति //
9.2.4.m: While it is being suffocated, he offers three oblations with: "To the out-breath svāhā!", "To the in-breath svāhā!", "To the diffused breath svāhā!"

9.2.4.s: amby ambike \\ iti mahiṣīm abhyudānayati tūṣṇīm itare śatam̐ sārdhaṃ patnyā /
9.2.4.d: अम्ब्य् अम्बिके \\ इति महिषीम् अभ्युदानयति तूष्णीम् इतरे शतम्̐ सार्धं पत्न्या /
9.2.4.m: With: "O mother, little mother..." he brings the chief queen forward; the other [women], a hundred along with the wife, [come forward] silently.

9.2.4.s: vihatya keśān udgrathya savyān dakṣiṇān ūrūn ghnānās \\ gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatim̐ havāmahe \\ iti dakṣiṇapādam aśvaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ triḥ pariyanty udgrathya dakṣiṇān keśān udakpādam̐ savyān ūrūn ghnānāḥ prasavyaṃ triḥ pariyanti //
9.2.4.d: विहत्य केशान् उद्ग्रथ्य सव्यान् दक्षिणान् ऊरून् घ्नानास् \\ गणानां त्वा गणपतिम्̐ हवामहे \\ इति दक्षिणपादम् अश्वं प्रदक्षिणं त्रिः परियन्त्य् उद्ग्रथ्य दक्षिणान् केशान् उदक्पादम्̐ सव्यान् ऊरून् घ्नानाः प्रसव्यं त्रिः परियन्ति //
9.2.4.m: Having untied their hair and knotted it on the left, beating their right thighs, with: "We invoke you, lord of the hosts of hosts...", they circumambulate the horse three times clockwise keeping it on their right side; having knotted their hair on the right, beating their left thighs, they go around it three times counter-clockwise, facing north.

9.2.4.s: vaso mama \\ iti pādāny aghrati pariśrite /
9.2.4.d: वसो मम \\ इति पादान्य् अघ्रति परिश्रिते /
9.2.4.m: In the enclosed space, [the wife] smells the feet [of the horse] with: "O my treasure..."

9.2.4.s: avākśirasam uttānam āham ajāni garbhadham iti patny aśvam abhimedhati //
9.2.4.d: अवाक्शिरसम् उत्तानम् आहम् अजानि गर्भधम् इति पत्न्य् अश्वम् अभिमेधति //
9.2.4.m: Lying supine with her head downwards, the wife approaches the horse sexually with: "I will insert the seed-bearer..."

9.2.4.s: dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam ity ucchritāyām̐ sarve japanti /
9.2.4.d: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषम् इत्य् उच्छ्रितायाम्̐ सर्वे जपन्ति /
9.2.4.m: When she has stood up, all mutter: "I have praised Dadhikrāvan..."

9.2.4.s: pratyakśirasaḥ sūcībhiḥ patnyo 'sipathān kalpayanti gāyatrī triṣṭub iti dvābhyāṃ mahiṣī sauvarṇībhir ā hanubhyāṃ bhṛdayāt kroḍād uttarābhyām̐ vāvātā rājatībhir ā puchāt /
9.2.4.d: प्रत्यक्शिरसः सूचीभिः पत्न्यो ऽसिपथान् कल्पयन्ति गायत्री त्रिष्टुब् इति द्वाभ्यां महिषी सौवर्णीभिर् आ हनुभ्यां भृदयात् क्रोडाद् उत्तराभ्याम्̐ वावाता राजतीभिर् आ पुछात् /
9.2.4.m: While [the horse] lies with its head to the west, the wives trace the paths for the knife with needles: with the two [formulas] "The gāyatrī, the triṣṭubh..." the chief queen with golden ones from the jaws to the breast; with the two subsequent ones, the favorite wife with silver ones from the chest to the tail.

9.2.4.s: nāśvasya vapā / candra iti meda ācakṣate tataś coddharanti /
9.2.4.d: नाश्वस्य वपा / चन्द्र इति मेद आचक्षते ततश् चोद्धरन्ति /
9.2.4.m: The horse has no omentum (vapā). They call the fat "candra" (the moon); and from there they extract it.

9.2.4.s: uttarato 'śvasya candram̐ śrapayati /
9.2.4.d: उत्तरतो ऽश्वस्य चन्द्रम्̐ श्रपयति /
9.2.4.m: To the north of the horse, he cooks the candra.

9.2.4.s:
ekas tvaṣṭur aśvasyā viśastā \ dvā yantārā bhavatas tathā ṛtuḥ /
yā te gātrāṇām ṛtuthā kṛṇomi \ tātā piṇḍānāṃ pra juhomy agnau //
svāhā \\ ity āhavanīye trīñ śṛtapaiṇḍān ādadhāti /
9.2.4.d:
एकस् त्वष्टुर् अश्वस्या विशस्ता \ द्वा यन्तारा भवतस् तथा ऋतुः /
या ते गात्राणाम् ऋतुथा कृणोमि \ ताता पिण्डानां प्र जुहोम्य् अग्नौ //
स्वाहा \\ इत्य् आहवनीये त्रीञ् शृतपैण्डान् आदधाति /
9.2.4.m:
"Tvaṣṭṛ has one slaughterer of the horse, / Two are the restrainers; thus is the season.

Whatever limbs of yours I prepare in the seasonal order, / Those portions of balls I offer into the fire."

With: "Svāhā!" he deposits three cooked balls into the āhavanīya fire.

9.2.4.s: uttarato 'śvasya vaitase kaṭe 'vadāyātikramyetarayor avadyati /
9.2.4.d: उत्तरतो ऽश्वस्य वैतसे कटे ऽवदायातिक्रम्येतरयोर् अवद्यति /
9.2.4.m: To the north of the horse, having cut portions onto a reed mat and having stepped across, he cuts portions of the other two [victims].

9.2.4.s: abhito vapāṃ mahimānau juhoti svāhā devebhyas \\ iti purastāt sauvarṇena viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā \\ ity upariṣṭād rājatena //
9.2.4.d: अभितो वपां महिमानौ जुहोति स्वाहा देवेभ्यस् \\ इति पुरस्तात् सौवर्णेन विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहा \\ इत्य् उपरिष्टाद् राजतेन //
9.2.4.m: On both sides of the omentum, he offers the two Mahiman libations: before, with a golden [vessel], with "Svāhā to the gods!"; after, with a silver [vessel], with "Svāhā to the Viśve Devas!"

9.2.4.s: prajāpataye \\ ity upām̐śu hayasya chāgasyosrasya candravapānāṃ medaso 'nubrūhi \\ ity anuvācayati /
9.2.4.d: प्रजापतये \\ इत्य् उपाम्̐शु हयस्य छागस्योस्रस्य चन्द्रवपानां मेदसो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् अनुवाचयति /
9.2.4.m: He causes [the hotṛ] to recite in a whisper: "To Prajāpati... recite [the invitatory verse] for the fat of the candra-omentum of the horse, of the goat, [and] of the bull."

9.2.4.s: āśrāvya prajāpataye \\ ity upām̐śu hayasya chāgasyosrasya candravapānāṃ medasaḥ preṣya \\ iti pracarati /
9.2.4.d: आश्राव्य प्रजापतये \\ इत्य् उपाम्̐शु हयस्य छागस्योस्रस्य चन्द्रवपानां मेदसः प्रेष्य \\ इति प्रचरति /
9.2.4.m: Having called for the śrauta call, he proceeds [saying]: 'To Prajāpati,' in a whisper, 'urge [the hotṛ] for the omenta and fat of the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox!'

9.2.4.s: yathāvadānam̐ samavadāyottareṣāṃ paśūnām \\ viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ chāgānāṃ meṣāṇām usrāṇām̐ vapānāṃ medaso 'nubrūhi \\ ity anuvācayati /
9.2.4.d: यथावदानम्̐ समवदायोत्तरेषां पशूनाम् \\ विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः छागानां मेषाणाम् उस्राणाम्̐ वपानां मेदसो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् अनुवाचयति /
9.2.4.m: Having cut the portions in the prescribed manner from the subsequent animals, he bids [the hotṛ] recite: 'For the All-Gods, recite [the invitatory verse] for the omenta and fat of the hornless goats, the rams, and the wild oxen!'

9.2.4.s: āśrāvya viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ chāgānāṃ meṣāṇām usrāṇām̐ vapānāṃ medasaḥ preṣya \\ iti pracarati /
9.2.4.d: आश्राव्य विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः छागानां मेषाणाम् उस्राणाम्̐ वपानां मेदसः प्रेष्य \\ इति प्रचरति /
9.2.4.m: Having called for the śrauta call, he proceeds [saying]: 'For the All-Gods, urge [the hotṛ] for the omenta and fat of the hornless goats, the rams, and the wild oxen!'

9.2.4.s: sūkaravikartaṃ prajāpatyam̐ viśasanti /
9.2.4.d: सूकरविकर्तं प्रजापत्यम्̐ विशसन्ति /
9.2.4.m: They dissect the victims dedicated to Prajāpati [as in] the dissection of a boar.

9.2.4.s: uttarato 'śvasya śoṇitam̐ śrapayati / śoṇite tejanīty ācakṣate /
9.2.4.d: उत्तरतो ऽश्वस्य शोणितम्̐ श्रपयति / शोणिते तेजनीत्य् आचक्षते /
9.2.4.m: He cooks the blood of the horse to the north. They call the blood 'the sharp fire.'

9.2.4.s: avadānāny avadāyāvadānaśaḥ prājāpatyāñ śrapayanti /
9.2.4.d: अवदानान्य् अवदायावदानशः प्राजापत्याञ् श्रपयन्ति /
9.2.4.m: Having cut the portions portion by portion, they cook the portions of the victims dedicated to Prajāpati.

9.2.4.s: śūlyam aśvasya kuryāt /
9.2.4.d: शूल्यम् अश्वस्य कुर्यात् /

9.2.5.s: siddham ā dakṣiṇākālāt /
9.2.5.d: सिद्धम् आ दक्षिणाकालात् /
9.2.5.m: [The ritual] is established up to the time of the sacrificial gift.

9.2.5.s: kāmaprāptā dakṣiṇā dadāti yadi kāmam āvayet /
9.2.5.d: कामप्राप्ता दक्षिणा ददाति यदि कामम् आवयेत् /
9.2.5.m: He gives a sacrificial gift obtained according to desire, if he should invite desired objects.

9.2.5.s: yat prācyāṃ diśy abrāhmaṇānām̐ vittam̐ syāt tad adhvaryave dadyāt kṣetradvipadavarjam̐ yad dakṣiṇasyāṃ tad brahmaṇe yat pratīcyāṃ tad dhotre yad udīcyāṃ tad udgātre /
9.2.5.d: यत् प्राच्यां दिश्य् अब्राह्मणानाम्̐ वित्तम्̐ स्यात् तद् अध्वर्यवे दद्यात् क्षेत्रद्विपदवर्जम्̐ यद् दक्षिणस्यां तद् ब्रह्मणे यत् प्रतीच्यां तद् धोत्रे यद् उदीच्यां तद् उद्गात्रे /
9.2.5.m: Whatever property of non-Brahmins may be in the eastern quarter, that he should give to the adhvaryu priest, excluding land and two-footed beings [slaves]; whatever is in the southern, to the brahman priest; whatever is in the western, to the hotṛ priest; whatever is in the northern, to the udgātṛ priest.

9.2.5.s: māhendraṃ gṛhītvā stotram upākaroti //
9.2.5.d: माहेन्द्रं गृहीत्वा स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति //
9.2.5.m: Having drawn the Māhendra cup, he brings near the chant.

9.2.5.s: agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase \\ iti saptānāṃ prathamās tāḥ purastād abhiṣekasya kuryāt prajāpatiś carati garbhe antar iti saptānāṃ prathamās tāḥ purastāt prāṇabhṛta upariṣṭād apānabhṛtaḥ /
9.2.5.d: अग्न आयूम्̐षि पवसे \\ इति सप्तानां प्रथमास् ताः पुरस्ताद् अभिषेकस्य कुर्यात् प्रजापतिश् चरति गर्भे अन्तर् इति सप्तानां प्रथमास् ताः पुरस्तात् प्राणभृत उपरिष्टाद् अपानभृतः /
9.2.5.m: 'Agni, thou purifiest the spans of life'—these are the first of seven [formulas]; he should perform those before the royal unction; 'Prajāpati moves within the womb'—these are the first of seven; those [are performed] before the prāṇabhṛt [offerings] and after the apānabhṛt [offerings].

9.2.5.s: sim̐hacarmaṇy abhiṣicyate /
9.2.5.d: सिम्̐हचर्मण्य् अभिषिच्यते /
9.2.5.m: He is anointed upon a lion skin.

9.2.5.s: ṛṣabhacarmopariṣṭād dhriyate //
9.2.5.d: ऋषभचर्मोपरिष्टाद् ध्रियते //
9.2.5.m: A bull skin is held above [him].

9.2.5.s: sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabho jātavedās \\ iti sauvarṇam̐ rukmam upariṣṭād dhārayan saṃpātenābhiṣiñcati prajāpatiṃ pārameṣṭhyāya \\ iti yathākāmam //
9.2.5.d: सहस्रशृङ्गो वृषभो जातवेदास् \\ इति सौवर्णम्̐ रुक्मम् उपरिष्टाद् धारयन् संपातेनाभिषिञ्चति प्रजापतिं पारमेष्ठ्याय \\ इति यथाकामम् //
9.2.5.m: Holding a gold ornament above with the mantra 'The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas...', he anoints him with the remaining drops, reciting 'Prajāpati for supreme lordship...' according to desire.

9.2.5.s: samiddho añjan kṛdaraṃ matīnām ity āprībhir hastaṃ gṛhṇāti /
9.2.5.d: समिद्धो अञ्जन् कृदरं मतीनाम् इत्य् आप्रीभिर् हस्तं गृह्णाति /
9.2.5.m: With the Āprī verses, beginning with 'Kindled, anointing the chamber of prayers...', he takes [his] hand.

9.2.5.s:
vi rakṣo vi mṛdho jahi \ vi vṛtrasya hanū ruja /
vi manyum indra vṛtrahann \ amitrasya śiro jahi //
iti mukham̐ vimṛṣṭe /
9.2.5.d:
वि रक्षो वि मृधो जहि \ वि वृत्रस्य हनू रुज /
वि मन्युम् इन्द्र वृत्रहन्न् \ अमित्रस्य शिरो जहि //
इति मुखम्̐ विमृष्टे /
9.2.5.m:
'Smite away the demon, smite away the adversaries, break apart Vṛtra's jaws!

Dispel the fury, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra; smash the enemy's head!'

9.2.5.s: jāgatān viṣṇukramān krāmati /
9.2.5.d: जागतान् विष्णुक्रमान् क्रामति /
9.2.5.m: He strides the Viṣṇukrama strides in the Jagatī meter.

9.2.5.s: māsanāmāni juhoti /
9.2.5.d: मासनामानि जुहोति /

9.2.5.s: uttarato 'śvasya vaitase kaṭe 'vadyati /
9.2.5.d: उत्तरतो ऽश्वस्य वैतसे कटे ऽवद्यति /
9.2.5.m: To the north of the horse, he cuts the portions on a reed mat.

9.2.5.s: gomṛgakaṇṭhena tejanyām̐ sviṣṭakṛto vaṣaṭkāro juhoti /
9.2.5.d: गोमृगकण्ठेन तेजन्याम्̐ स्विष्टकृतो वषट्कारो जुहोति /
9.2.5.m: With the throat of the gomṛga upon the sharp fire, the vaṣaṭ-call of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering [is made], and he offers.

9.2.5.s: aśvaśaphena patnīsam̐yājayaty ayasmayena varuṇāvabhṛtheṣṭau /
9.2.5.d: अश्वशफेन पत्नीसम्̐याजयत्य् अयस्मयेन वरुणावभृथेष्टौ /
9.2.5.m: With a horse hoof made of iron, he makes the patnīsaṃyāja offerings in the avabhṛtha offering of Varuṇa.

9.2.5.s: vaitase kaṭe prājāpatyān saṃcinoti prāñcāv aśvatūparau pratyañcaṃ gomṛgam /
9.2.5.d: वैतसे कटे प्राजापत्यान् संचिनोति प्राञ्चाव् अश्वतूपरौ प्रत्यञ्चं गोमृगम् /
9.2.5.m: On a reed mat he arranges the victims dedicated to Prajāpati: the horse and the hornless goat facing east, and the gomṛga facing west.

9.2.5.s: vaṣaṭkṛte rājaputrāś catvāra ādadhaty āhavanīye /
9.2.5.d: वषट्कृते राजपुत्राश् चत्वार आदधत्य् आहवनीये /
9.2.5.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, four princes place [them] on the āhavanīya fire.

9.2.5.s: pratyāhutyājyaṃ gṛhītvā śādaṃ dadbhiḥ svāhā yasyāraṇye 'dhītenānuvākena //
9.2.5.d: प्रत्याहुत्याज्यं गृहीत्वा शादं दद्भिः स्वाहा यस्यारण्ये ऽधीतेनानुवाकेन //
9.2.5.m: Having taken clarified butter for each offering, [he offers] with the chapter learned in the forest beginning with 'Grass with the teeth, svāhā...'

9.2.5.s: mā no mitro varuṇas \\ ity aśvastomīyāḥ ṣoḍaśāhutīr juhoti /
9.2.5.d: मा नो मित्रो वरुणस् \\ इत्य् अश्वस्तोमीयाः षोडशाहुतीर् जुहोति /
9.2.5.m: With the mantra 'May not Mitra, Varuṇa...', he offers sixteen Aśvastomīya oblations.

9.2.5.s: siddha upavasathaḥ /
9.2.5.d: सिद्ध उपवसथः /

9.2.5.s: śvobhūte sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ /
9.2.5.d: श्वोभूते सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.2.5.m: On the next day, there is the Atirātra sacrifice containing all stomas.

9.2.5.s: siddham opākaraṇāt /
9.2.5.d: सिद्धम् ओपाकरणात् /

9.2.5.s: gavyān aikādaśinān upākaroti /
9.2.5.d: गव्यान् ऐकादशिनान् उपाकरोति /
9.2.5.m: He drives up the eleven bovine victims.

9.2.5.s: siddham āvabhṛthāt /
9.2.5.d: सिद्धम् आवभृथात् /

9.2.5.s: durmagadasyāsyadaghna udake 'vasthitasya jumbakāya svāhā \\ iti mūrdhani tisra āhutīrjuhoti mṛtyave svāhā \\ ity apsu brahmahatyāyai svāhā \\ iti dvitīyām /
9.2.5.d: दुर्मगदस्यास्यदघ्न उदके ऽवस्थितस्य जुम्बकाय स्वाहा \\ इति मूर्धनि तिस्र आहुतीर्जुहोति मृत्यवे स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अप्सु ब्रह्महत्यायै स्वाहा \\ इति द्वितीयाम् /
9.2.5.m: Upon the head of a white-spotted, bald-headed man standing in mouth-deep water, he offers three oblations with 'To Jumbaka, svāhā!'; into the waters with 'To Death, svāhā!'; a second one with 'To Brahmin-murder, svāhā!'

9.2.5.s: tarati mṛtyuṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ tarati brahmahatyām̐ yo 'śvamedhena yajate yaś caivam̐ veda /
9.2.5.d: तरति मृत्युं तरति पाप्मानं तरति ब्रह्महत्याम्̐ यो ऽश्वमेधेन यजते यश् चैवम्̐ वेद /
9.2.5.m: He crosses beyond death, he crosses beyond evil, he crosses beyond Brahmin-murder, whoever sacrifices with the horse sacrifice and whoever knows thus.

9.2.5.s: yāvanto 'śvasya hūyamānasya gandham avajighranti sarve te puṇyalokā bhavanti /
9.2.5.d: यावन्तो ऽश्वस्य हूयमानस्य गन्धम् अवजिघ्रन्ति सर्वे ते पुण्यलोका भवन्ति /
9.2.5.m: As many as smell the scent of the horse being offered, all of them attain meritorious worlds.

9.2.5.s: siddham ānūbandhyāyāḥ /
9.2.5.d: सिद्धम् आनूबन्ध्यायाः /
9.2.5.m: [The procedure] is established up to the anūbandhyā cow.

9.2.5.s: nava saurīḥ śvetā anūbandhyās tāsām̐ vapāsu hūyamānāsu prativātaṃ tiṣṭheran mucyante pāpakṛtaḥ /
9.2.5.d: नव सौरीः श्वेता अनूबन्ध्यास् तासाम्̐ वपासु हूयमानासु प्रतिवातं तिष्ठेरन् मुच्यन्ते पापकृतः /
9.2.5.m: There are nine white anūbandhyā cows dedicated to Sūrya; while their omenta are being offered, the evil-doers should stand against the wind: they are freed [from sin].

9.2.5.s: tāsāṃ paśupuroḍāśam anu \\ am̐homuce \\ iti daśahaviṣā mṛgāreṣṭiṃ nirvapati /
9.2.5.d: तासां पशुपुरोडाशम् अनु \\ अम्̐होमुचे \\ इति दशहविषा मृगारेष्टिं निर्वपति /
9.2.5.m: Following the animal sacrificial cake for these, he apportions the Mṛgāreṣṭi with ten oblations, beginning with 'To the deliverer from distress...'

9.2.5.s: sarvapṛṣṭhayā bhūtikāmo yajetābhiśasyamāno vā / bibhyan mṛgāreṣṭyāmayāvī vā /
9.2.5.d: सर्वपृष्ठया भूतिकामो यजेताभिशस्यमानो वा / बिभ्यन् मृगारेष्ट्यामयावी वा /
9.2.5.m: One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the Sarvapṛṣṭhā sacrifice, or one being falsely accused; or one who is afraid or sick should sacrifice with the Mṛgāreṣṭi.

9.2.5.s: udagudavasāyātraitān kālābhrūnajān anupūrvam̐ vai triśākhe niyojaned āgneyaṃ madhyama aindraṃ dakṣiṇa āśvinam uttare /
9.2.5.d: उदगुदवसायात्रैतान् कालाभ्रूनजान् अनुपूर्वम्̐ वै त्रिशाखे नियोजनेद् आग्नेयं मध्यम ऐन्द्रं दक्षिण आश्विनम् उत्तरे /
9.2.5.m: Having departed northward, he should bind these black, brown goats in sequence to a three-branched post: the one for Agni on the middle [branch], the one for Indra on the southern, the one for the Aśvins on the northern.

9.2.5.s: siddhaḥ paśubandhaḥ /
9.2.5.d: सिद्धः पशुबन्धः /

9.2.5.s: dvādaśa brahmaudanān paktvā madhyataḥkāribhyo dadyāt tebhyo dvādaśa ca dhenūḥ /
9.2.5.d: द्वादश ब्रह्मौदनान् पक्त्वा मध्यतःकारिभ्यो दद्यात् तेभ्यो द्वादश च धेनूः /
9.2.5.m: Having cooked twelve brahmaudana portions, he should give them to the central officiants, and twelve milch cows to them.

9.2.5.s: api vā devikābhir iṣṭvā mṛgāreṣṭyā yajeta yajeta /
9.2.5.d: अपि वा देविकाभिर् इष्ट्वा मृगारेष्ट्या यजेत यजेत /
9.2.5.m: Alternatively, having sacrificed with the Devikā oblations, he should sacrifice with the Mṛgāreṣṭi—he should sacrifice.

9.3.1.m: The rule for the one-day rites is traditionally handed down.

9.3.1.s: sāgnayaḥ sarve 'nyatṣoḍaśitīvrasuccāturmāsyebhyo yeṣām anāgnikyo dīkṣā upasadaḥ /
9.3.1.d: साग्नयः सर्वे ऽन्यत्षोडशितीव्रसुच्चातुर्मास्येभ्यो येषाम् अनाग्निक्यो दीक्षा उपसदः /
9.3.1.m: All [one-day rites] possess the sacred fires, except the Ṣoḍaśin, the Tīvrasut, and the Cāturmāsya rites, which have consecrations and upasads without the sacred fires.

9.3.1.s: kāmo yeṣu prajā paśavaḥ prajātir vā pravargyās teṣu prākṛtaśvokthaḥ /
9.3.1.d: कामो येषु प्रजा पशवः प्रजातिर् वा प्रवर्ग्यास् तेषु प्राकृतश्वोक्थः /
9.3.1.m: Those rites in which the desired object is offspring, cattle, or procreation, have the Pravargya; in them the uktha is the original one.

9.3.1.s: rathaṃtare rathaṃtaravarṇe vaindravāyavāgraṃ bṛhati bṛhadvarṇe vā śukrāgram̐ vāmadevye vāmadevyavarṇe vāgrāyaṇāgram /
9.3.1.d: रथंतरे रथंतरवर्णे वैन्द्रवायवाग्रं बृहति बृहद्वर्णे वा शुक्राग्रम्̐ वामदेव्ये वामदेव्यवर्णे वाग्रायणाग्रम् /
9.3.1.m: When the Rathantara is the pṛṣṭha chant, or of the Rathantara nature, the Aindravāyava cup is first; when the Bṛhat, or of the Bṛhat nature, the Śukra cup is first; when the Vāmadevya, or of the Vāmadevya nature, the Āgrayaṇa cup is first.
In a sacrifice with a thousand sacrificial gifts, he draws the Pṛṣṭhya Atigrāhya cups.

9.3.1.s: anūbandhyā maitrāvaruṇī vaiśvadevī bārhaspatyā / tāsāṃ parisaṃkhyā yathām̐śvadābhyayor vājapeye /
9.3.1.d: अनूबन्ध्या मैत्रावरुणी वैश्वदेवी बार्हस्पत्या / तासां परिसंख्या यथाम्̐श्वदाभ्ययोर् वाजपेये /
9.3.1.m: The anūbandhyā victims are dedicated to Mitra-Varuṇa, the All-Gods, and Bṛhaspati; their restriction is like that of the Aṃśu and Adābhya cups in the Vājapeya sacrifice.

9.3.1.s: sahasradakṣiṇena yakṣyamāṇa iṣṭvā ca traidhātavyayā yajeta /
9.3.1.d: सहस्रदक्षिणेन यक्ष्यमाण इष्ट्वा च त्रैधातव्यया यजेत /
9.3.1.m: Intending to sacrifice with a rite requiring a thousand sacrificial gifts, and having sacrificed, he should sacrifice with the Traidhātavīyā offering.
Articles of use, a milch cow, and gold are the sacrificial gift.
In the absence of an explicit rule, however, the completion is that of the Agniṣṭoma.
The Trikadruka rites of Indra have the Rathantara as their pṛṣṭha chant.

9.3.1.s: jyotiṣṭomena svargakāmo yajetemaṃ ca lokam abhijigīṣan /
9.3.1.d: ज्योतिष्टोमेन स्वर्गकामो यजेतेमं च लोकम् अभिजिगीषन् /
9.3.1.m: One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma, also one wishing to conquer this world.
The Agniṣṭoma has the uktha chant. One desiring all cattle should sacrifice, wishing to conquer the world of the intermediate region.

9.3.1.s: āyuṣṭoma ukthyaḥ / sarvakāmo yajetāmuṃ ca lokam abhijigīṣan /
9.3.1.d: आयुष्टोम उक्थ्यः / सर्वकामो यजेतामुं च लोकम् अभिजिगीषन् /
9.3.1.m: The Āyuṣṭoma has the Ukthya ending. One desiring everything should sacrifice, wishing to conquer yonder world.
One wishing to conquer the conquest of the unconquered should sacrifice with the Abhijit of Indra; it has both sāmans and the Rathantara as its pṛṣṭha chant.

9.3.1.s: indrasya viśvajit sarvapṛṣṭho viśvam abhijigīṣan yajeta /
9.3.1.d: इन्द्रस्य विश्वजित् सर्वपृष्ठो विश्वम् अभिजिगीषन् यजेत /
9.3.1.m: One wishing to conquer all should sacrifice with Indra's Viśvajit, having all pṛṣṭhas.

9.3.1.s: purā prātaranuvākād yajamānaḥ sauvarṇīm̐ śatamānīṃ dvādaśapuṇḍarīkāṃ mālāṃ pratimuñcate /
9.3.1.d: पुरा प्रातरनुवाकाद् यजमानः सौवर्णीम्̐ शतमानीं द्वादशपुण्डरीकां मालां प्रतिमुञ्चते /
9.3.1.m: Before the morning recitation, the sacrificer puts on a golden garland weighing a hundred mānas, having twelve lotuses.
He draws the pṛṣṭhya atigrāhya cups.

9.3.1.s: tān anupṛṣṭhaṃ juhoti kriyante ca pṛṣṭhyaśilpāni /
9.3.1.d: तान् अनुपृष्ठं जुहोति क्रियन्ते च पृष्ठ्यशिल्पानि /
9.3.1.m: He offers them after the pṛṣṭhas, and the pṛṣṭhya-śilpa chants are performed.
At the time of sacrificial gifts, he gives all his possessions and the garland.
The hotṛ's chant is the Vairāja, having the tune of the Bṛhat.

9.3.1.s: avabhṛthād udetya sakarṇapuchām̐ sarvakalām̐ rohiṇīm̐ vatsatvacam āchādayate /
9.3.1.d: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य सकर्णपुछाम्̐ सर्वकलाम्̐ रोहिणीम्̐ वत्सत्वचम् आछादयते /
9.3.1.m: Having stepped out of the purificatory bath, he puts on a red calf-skin complete with ears and tail and fully intact.

9.3.1.s: sam̐sthāpyodavasānīyām uṣṇīṣy adhaḥśayo 'mṛtpātram ubhayatastīkṣṇām abhrim audumbarīm ādāya khanitrajīvana audumbare tisro rātrīr vasati /
9.3.1.d: सम्̐स्थाप्योदवसानीयाम् उष्णीष्य् अधःशयो ऽमृत्पात्रम् उभयतस्तीक्ष्णाम् अभ्रिम् औदुम्बरीम् आदाय खनित्रजीवन औदुम्बरे तिस्रो रात्रीर् वसति /
9.3.1.m: Having concluded the udavasānīyā rite, wearing a turban, sleeping on the ground, having a non-earthen vessel, taking an audumbara spade sharpened at both ends, living by digging, he resides for three nights in an audumbara grove.
They have both sāmans, with the Bṛhat as pṛṣṭha.

9.3.2.s: teṣām ādityānāṃ trivṛt prathamo bhrātṛvyavān svargakāmaḥ paśukāmo yajeta /
9.3.2.d: तेषाम् आदित्यानां त्रिवृत् प्रथमो भ्रातृव्यवान् स्वर्गकामः पशुकामो यजेत /
9.3.2.m: Of them, the first belongs to the Ādityas, is ninefold; one who has a rival, one who desires heaven, or one who desires cattle should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.2.s: mahārātre kṣīradṛtīn aśvaratheṣv ādhāyartvijaḥ samānayanti / ... yujodgātāraṃ paścād dvikrośād dviyujā hotāraṃ dakṣiṇataḥ krośāt sthūriṇā brahmāṇam /
9.3.2.d: महारात्रे क्षीरदृतीन् अश्वरथेष्व् आधायर्त्विजः समानयन्ति / ... युजोद्गातारं पश्चाद् द्विक्रोशाद् द्वियुजा होतारं दक्षिणतः क्रोशात् स्थूरिणा ब्रह्माणम् /
9.3.2.m: In the dead of night, having placed leather milk-bags on horse-drawn chariots, they bring together the officiating priests: [the adhvaryu bringing] the udgātṛ with a chariot yoked with […] from two krośas to the west, the hotṛ with a two-yoked [chariot] from one krośa to the south, the brahman with a single-horse chariot.
They perform everything in a single day.
An uncastrated three-year-old bull is the purchase-price for soma.
At the Upasads, having closed their eyes, they proceed at three places.

9.3.2.s: cātvāladeśe lāṅgaleṣāṃ khalevālīṃ nihatya yavān kṛṣanti / teṣām uttaravediṃ dhiṣṇyāṃś ca nivapanti /
9.3.2.d: चात्वालदेशे लाङ्गलेषां खलेवालीं निहत्य यवान् कृषन्ति / तेषाम् उत्तरवेदिं धिष्ण्यांश् च निवपन्ति /
9.3.2.m: At the place of the cātvāla, having driven in a post for a threshing floor as the plough-pole, they plough barley. They scatter the high altar and the dhiṣṇya hearths with them.

9.3.2.s: āvṛtya khalevālīṃ prokṣaṇaprabhṛti yūpaṃ kurvanti / yavakalāpi caṣālam /
9.3.2.d: आवृत्य खलेवालीं प्रोक्षणप्रभृति यूपं कुर्वन्ति / यवकलापि चषालम् /
9.3.2.m: Turning the post of the threshing floor, beginning with sprinkling, they make it the sacrificial post. A bundle of barley is the post-ring.

9.3.2.d: अग्नीषोमीयकाले ऽग्नीषोमीयेन पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्य वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति /
9.3.2.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma, having proceeded with the animal cake for Agni-Soma, he draws the vasatīvarī waters.

9.3.2.s: savanīyakāle yūpam̐ saṃmitya paśūn upākaroty agnīṣomīyam̐ savanīyam anūbandhyām /
9.3.2.d: सवनीयकाले यूपम्̐ संमित्य पशून् उपाकरोत्य् अग्नीषोमीयम्̐ सवनीयम् अनूबन्ध्याम् /
9.3.2.m: At the time of the pressings, having measured the sacrificial post, he brings forward the animals: the one for Agni-Soma, the one for the pressings, and the anūbandhyā cow.

9.3.2.d: दक्षिणाकाले ऽश्वम्̐ श्वेतम्̐ रुक्यप्रतिमुक्तम् आङ्गिरसायोद्गात्रे दद्यात् /
9.3.2.m: At the time of sacrificial gifts, he should give a white horse decorated with a gold ornament to the Āṅgirasa udgātṛ.
At the time of the anūbandhyā animal, there is a cake on one potsherd for Mitra-Varuṇa, or a curd offering.
For a year, he should not anoint his eyes, should not rub his body with oil, and should not wash his feet from above.
Having made the agniṣṭoma-sāman of this very [rite] twenty-one-fold, one desiring spiritual brilliance should sacrifice.

9.3.2.s: aṅgirasām anukrīrya ānujāvaro hīna iva syāt sa etena yajeta /
9.3.2.d: अङ्गिरसाम् अनुक्रीर्य आनुजावरो हीन इव स्यात् स एतेन यजेत /
9.3.2.m: The Anukrī of the Aṅgirases: one who is degenerate, who seems base, should sacrifice with this.

9.3.2.s: aśvam̐ śvetaṃ brahmaṇe dadāti piśaṅgīm̐ vaḍavām udgātre /
9.3.2.d: अश्वम्̐ श्वेतं ब्रह्मणे ददाति पिशङ्गीम्̐ वडवाम् उद्गात्रे /
9.3.2.m: He gives a white horse to the brahman, a reddish-brown mare to the udgātṛ.

9.3.2.s: viśveṣāṃ devānām̐ viśvajichilpaḥ sarvapṛṣṭhaḥ / sarvakāmo yajeta / yathā viśvajit /
9.3.2.d: विश्वेषां देवानाम्̐ विश्वजिछिल्पः सर्वपृष्ठः / सर्वकामो यजेत / यथा विश्वजित् /
9.3.2.m: The Viśvajichilpa belongs to the Viśve Devas, having all pṛṣṭhas. One desiring all should sacrifice. [It is performed] like the Viśvajit.
Indra's Śyena, or Vasiṣṭha's: one practising sorcery should sacrifice [with it].
He should settle on barren ground, or on ploughed land left unsown.

9.3.2.s: lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā nivītā ṛtvijaḥ khaḍgapāṇayaḥ pāruṣyanta iva pracaranti /
9.3.2.d: लोहितोष्णीषा लोहितवसना निवीता ऋत्विजः खड्गपाणयः पारुष्यन्त इव प्रचरन्ति /
9.3.2.m: Wearing red turbans, red garments, wearing the sacred thread suspended straight around their necks, sword in hand, the officiating priests proceed as if about to do violence.

9.3.2.s: rathau havirdhāne nivartayitvopāñjanti śavavahanam abhyetyādhiṣavaṇaphalake gor anustaraṇikyāś carmādhiṣavaṇam /
9.3.2.d: रथौ हविर्धाने निवर्तयित्वोपाञ्जन्ति शववहनम् अभ्येत्याधिषवणफलके गोर् अनुस्तरणिक्याश् चर्माधिषवणम् /
9.3.2.m: Having turned back the two carts, they anoint them; having approached the hearse, the pressing-boards [are made from it]; the skin of the cow slaughtered for the corpse is the pressing-skin.

9.3.2.s: sphyāgro yūpo 'caṣālas tailvako bādhako vā / śaramayaṃ barhir vaibhītaka idhmaḥ /
9.3.2.d: स्फ्याग्रो यूपो ऽचषालस् तैल्वको बाधको वा / शरमयं बर्हिर् वैभीतक इध्मः /
9.3.2.m: The sacrificial post has the tip of a wooden sword, lacks a post-ring, and is made of tilvaka or bādhaka wood. The sacrificial grass is made of reed-grass; the sacrificial fuel is of vibhītaka wood.
He deposits cups beginning with the manthin cup before the āgrāyaṇa cup.
A red goat is the victim for the pressing, offered to Agni accompanied by Rudra.
He gives nine [cows] each as sacrificial gifts.

9.3.2.s: prajāpater udbhid ekatrika eṣāṃ lokānām udbhidbhiḥ sam̐yajeta /
9.3.2.d: प्रजापतेर् उद्भिद् एकत्रिक एषां लोकानाम् उद्भिद्भिः सम्̐यजेत /
9.3.2.m: Prajāpati's Udbhid: [it is an] ekatrika; he should sacrifice together with the conquerors of these worlds.

9.3.3.s: devānāṃ prathamo vrātyastomaś catuḥṣoḍaśī /
9.3.3.d: देवानां प्रथमो व्रात्यस्तोमश् चतुःषोडशी /
9.3.3.m: The first Vrātyastoma belongs to the gods; it has four ṣoḍaśin cups.

9.3.3.s: śrotriyān vrātyām̐ś catvāri pāvanārtham̐ yajeran /
9.3.3.d: श्रोत्रियान् व्रात्याम्̐श् चत्वारि पावनार्थम्̐ यजेरन् /
9.3.3.m: For Vrātyas who are learned in the Veda, they should perform four [Vrātyastomas] for the sake of purification.

9.3.3.s: teṣām̐ vyañjanāny uṣṇīṣaṃ pratodo jyāhroḍo ratho vipathaḥ phalakās tīrṇaḥ kṛṣṇadaśam̐ vāso nīlabalakṣe ajine rājato rukmas tad gṛhapateḥ /
9.3.3.d: तेषाम्̐ व्यञ्जनान्य् उष्णीषं प्रतोदो ज्याह्रोडो रथो विपथः फलकास् तीर्णः कृष्णदशम्̐ वासो नीलबलक्षे अजिने राजतो रुक्मस् तद् गृहपतेः /
9.3.3.m: Their emblems are: a turban, a goad, a bow without an arrow, an unpaved wagon covered with planks, a garment with black fringes, two black and white skins, a silver ornament—that belongs to the master of the house.

9.3.3.s: athetareṣāṃ dāmatūṣāṇi valūkāni lohitapramāṇāni dviṣaṃdhīny ajināni /
9.3.3.d: अथेतरेषां दामतूषाणि वलूकानि लोहितप्रमाणानि द्विषंधीन्य् अजिनानि /
9.3.3.m: Then, for the others, there are fringe-bordered garments, valūka sandals, red ornaments, and skins joined in pairs.

9.3.3.s: trayastrim̐śatātrayastrim̐śatā gṛhapatim abhi samāyanti /
9.3.3.d: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतात्रयस्त्रिम्̐शता गृहपतिम् अभि समायन्ति /
9.3.3.m: By thirty-threes they come together around the master of the house.

9.3.3.s: aśvaṃ catustrim̐śaṃ gṛhapater āharati /
9.3.3.d: अश्वं चतुस्त्रिम्̐शं गृहपतेर् आहरति /
9.3.3.m: He brings a horse as the thirty-fourth [gift] of the master of the house.

9.3.3.s: agnīn ādhāya gṛhapater agniṣu saṃnyupya yajeran /
9.3.3.d: अग्नीन् आधाय गृहपतेर् अग्निषु संन्युप्य यजेरन् /
9.3.3.m: Having established their sacred fires and poured them together into the fires of the master of the house, they should sacrifice.

9.3.3.s: siddham ā dakṣiṇākālāt /
9.3.3.d: सिद्धम् आ दक्षिणाकालात् /
9.3.3.m: The ritual is established up to the time of sacrificial gifts.

9.3.3.s: yaṃ divṣyāt tasmai vrātyaliṅgāni dadyād vrātyadhanaṃ ca / dakṣiṇaivam /
9.3.3.d: यं दिव्ष्यात् तस्मै व्रात्यलिङ्गानि दद्याद् व्रात्यधनं च / दक्षिणैवम् /
9.3.3.m: To whomever he hates, to him he should give the Vrātya insignia and the Vrātya wealth; that is the sacrificial gift.

9.3.3.s: nṛśam̐sā ninditā ukthyena ṣaṭṣoḍaśinā catuḥṣoḍaśinā / kaniṣṭhāḥ kāniṣṭhyena dviṣoḍaśinā / jyeṣṭhā jyaiṣṭhyena / jayaiṣṭhyakāmo yajeta /
9.3.3.d: नृशम्̐सा निन्दिता उक्थ्येन षट्षोडशिना चतुःषोडशिना / कनिष्ठाः कानिष्ठ्येन द्विषोडशिना / ज्येष्ठा ज्यैष्ठ्येन / जयैष्ठ्यकामो यजेत /
9.3.3.m: Cruel and censured men [sacrifice] with an ukthya having six ṣoḍaśin cups or four ṣoḍaśin cups; the youngest [sacrifice] with the Kāniṣṭhya having two ṣoḍaśin cups; the eldest with the Jyaiṣṭhya; one desiring seniority should sacrifice.

9.3.3.s: ubhayasāmā rathaṃtarapṛṣṭhaḥ /
9.3.3.d: उभयसामा रथंतरपृष्ठः /
9.3.3.m: It has both sāmans, with the Rathaṃtara as pṛṣṭha.

9.3.3.s: sarvastomenobhayasāmnā bṛhatpṛṣṭhenāgner agniṣṭutā /
9.3.3.d: सर्वस्तोमेनोभयसाम्ना बृहत्पृष्ठेनाग्नेर् अग्निष्टुता /
9.3.3.m: [The rite is] Agni's Agniṣṭut with all stomas, with both sāmans, having the Bṛhat as pṛṣṭha.

9.3.3.s: pravargyās teṣāṃ prathame 'gnyṛtam abhi śastrāṇi /
9.3.3.d: प्रवर्ग्यास् तेषां प्रथमे ऽग्न्यृतम् अभि शस्त्राणि /
9.3.3.m: They have the Pravargya; in the first of them, the recitations are directed toward Agni's sacred order.

9.3.3.s: trivṛd agniṣṭud agniṣṭomaḥ /
9.3.3.d: त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टुद् अग्निष्टोमः /
9.3.3.m: The Agniṣṭut is a ninefold agniṣṭoma.

9.3.3.s: tasya vāyavyāsv ekavim̐śam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā brahmavarcasakāmo yajeta /
9.3.3.d: तस्य वायव्यास्व् एकविम्̐शम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वा ब्रह्मवर्चसकामो यजेत /
9.3.3.m: Having made its agniṣṭoma-sāman twenty-one-fold on verses addressed to Vāyu, one desiring spiritual brilliance should sacrifice.

9.3.3.s: etasyaiva revatīṣu vāravantīyam agniṣṭomasāma kṛtvā paśukāmo yajeta /
9.3.3.d: एतस्यैव रेवतीषु वारवन्तीयम् अग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वा पशुकामो यजेत /
9.3.3.m: Having made the Vāravantīya the agniṣṭoma-sāman on the Revatī verses of this very [rite], one desiring cattle should sacrifice.

9.3.3.s: jyotiṣṭomenāgniṣṭutā yajñavibhraṣṭo yajeta yasmād vā stomād vibhram̐śeta /
9.3.3.d: ज्योतिष्टोमेनाग्निष्टुता यज्ञविभ्रष्टो यजेत यस्माद् वा स्तोमाद् विभ्रम्̐शेत /
9.3.3.m: One who has slipped from a sacrifice, or from whatever stoma he has slipped, should sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut as a Jyotiṣṭoma.

9.3.3.s: stomena saptadaśenāmayāvy annādyakāmaḥ pratiṣṭhākāmo vā yajeta /
9.3.3.d: स्तोमेन सप्तदशेनामयाव्य् अन्नाद्यकामः प्रतिष्ठाकामो वा यजेत /
9.3.3.m: One who is chronically ill, one who desires food, or one who desires a firm foundation should sacrifice with the seventeenfold stoma.

9.3.3.s: prajāpater apūrvas trivṛtā prathamo bhrātṛvyavān svargakāmaḥ paśukāmo vā yajeta /
9.3.3.d: प्रजापतेर् अपूर्वस् त्रिवृता प्रथमो भ्रातृव्यवान् स्वर्गकामः पशुकामो वा यजेत /
9.3.3.m: Prajāpati's Apūrva: the first is ninefold; one who has a rival, one who desires heaven, or one who desires cattle should sacrifice.

9.3.3.s: jamadagner iṣur abhicaran yajeta samānakalpaśyenam /
9.3.3.d: जमदग्नेर् इषुर् अभिचरन् यजेत समानकल्पश्येनम् /
9.3.3.m: One practicing sorcery should sacrifice with the Iṣu of Jamadagni; its procedure is identical to that of the Śyena.

9.3.3.s: bṛhaspatisavaḥ / purodhākāmaḥ sthāpatyakāmo brahmavarcasakāmo vā yajeta /
9.3.3.d: बृहस्पतिसवः / पुरोधाकामः स्थापत्यकामो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामो वा यजेत /
9.3.3.m: The Bṛhaspatisava. One desiring the office of domestic priest, desiring chiefmanship, or desiring spiritual luster should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.3.s: aruṇo mirmiraḥ parisragvī triśukriyaḥ /
9.3.3.d: अरुणो मिर्मिरः परिस्रग्वी त्रिशुक्रियः /
9.3.3.m: [The sacrificial animal is] reddish, blinking, wearing garlands, [or] threefold-white.

9.3.3.s: prātaḥsavane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣv ekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśati /
9.3.3.d: प्रातःसवने सन्नेषु नाराशम्̐सेष्व् एकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशति /
9.3.3.m: At the morning pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa [cups] are set down, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

9.3.3.s: aśvadvādaśā mādhyaṃdine vyādiśyobhayī dakṣiṇākāle 'tikālayati /
9.3.3.d: अश्वद्वादशा माध्यंदिने व्यादिश्योभयी दक्षिणाकाले ऽतिकालयति /
9.3.3.m: At the midday pressing, having assigned twelve, including a horse, he drives both [groups of animals] past at the time of the sacrificial gift.

9.3.3.s: māhendrakāle 'nuddhata ājyasya vājaprasavyam̐ hutvottaraveder āsandyām āsīnaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ purodhayā \\ iti yathākāmam abhiṣiñcati /
9.3.3.d: माहेन्द्रकाले ऽनुद्धत आज्यस्य वाजप्रसव्यम्̐ हुत्वोत्तरवेदेर् आसन्द्याम् आसीनं बृहस्पतिं पुरोधया \\ इति यथाकामम् अभिषिञ्चति /
9.3.3.m: At the time of the Māhendra [cup], on the unraised [ground], having offered the Vājaprasavya of clarified butter, he sprinkles [the sacrificer], seated on a wicker chair to the [rear] of the high altar, according to desire, with the mantra: 'Bṛhaspati with priesthood...'

9.3.3.s: tṛtīyasavane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣv ekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśati /
9.3.3.d: तृतीयसवने सन्नेषु नाराशम्̐सेष्व् एकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशति /
9.3.3.m: At the third pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa [cups] are set down, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

9.3.3.s: anūbandhyāyai dakṣiṇākāle 'tikālayati /
9.3.3.d: अनूबन्ध्यायै दक्षिणाकाले ऽतिकालयति /
9.3.3.m: At the time of the sacrificial gift for the Anūbandhyā [cow], he drives [them] past.

9.3.3.s: śunaskarṇastomaḥ sarvasvāro ya ichet sadyaḥ pretya svargam̐ lokam iyām iti sa etena yajeta /
9.3.3.d: शुनस्कर्णस्तोमः सर्वस्वारो य इछेत् सद्यः प्रेत्य स्वर्गम्̐ लोकम् इयाम् इति स एतेन यजेत /
9.3.3.m: The Śunaskarṇastoma, [which is] the Sarvasvāra. He who wishes, 'May I go immediately to the heavenly world having died,' he should sacrifice with this.

9.3.3.s: śuṇṭho 'jaḥ savanīyaḥ / kṛtānnaṃ dakṣiṇā / vāmadevyaṃ pṛṣṭham /
9.3.3.d: शुण्ठो ऽजः सवनीयः / कृतान्नं दक्षिणा / वामदेव्यं पृष्ठम् /
9.3.3.m: A gelded goat is the pressing-animal. Cooked food is the sacrificial gift. The Vāmadevya is the pṛṣṭha[-sāman].

9.3.3.s: ārbhave stūyamāne brāhmaṇāḥ sam̐sthāpayata me yajñam ity uktvā dakṣiṇata audumbaryā dakṣiṇāśirāḥ prāvṛto niṣadyate / tata eva saṃtiṣṭhate /
9.3.3.d: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने ब्राह्मणाः सम्̐स्थापयत मे यज्ञम् इत्य् उक्त्वा दक्षिणत औदुम्बर्या दक्षिणाशिराः प्रावृतो निषद्यते / तत एव संतिष्ठते /
9.3.3.m: While the Ārbhava[-stotra] is being chanted, having said: 'O brāhmaṇas, complete my sacrifice,' he sits down covered, with his head toward the south, to the south of the audumbarī post. Right there he passes away.

9.3.3.s: tasya bhakṣān mārjālīye ninayanti /
9.3.3.d: तस्य भक्षान् मार्जालीये निनयन्ति /
9.3.3.m: They pour his portions [of Soma] into the Mārjālīya fire.

9.3.3.s: avabhṛthavelāyām atīrthena nihṛtyāvabhṛthe praplāvyānyena vāsasā prachādya yathāsavyam̐ sam̐veśayanti /
9.3.3.d: अवभृथवेलायाम् अतीर्थेन निहृत्यावभृथे प्रप्लाव्यान्येन वाससा प्रछाद्य यथासव्यम्̐ सम्̐वेशयन्ति /
9.3.3.m: At the time of the purificatory bath, having carried him out through an improper way, having immersed him in the purificatory bath [water], and having covered him with another garment, they lay him down in the prescribed manner.

9.3.3.s: paryoṣaṇavelāyām āhavanīyād dahanti /
9.3.3.d: पर्योषणवेलायाम् आहवनीयाद् दहन्ति /
9.3.3.m: At the time of cremating, they burn him with the fire from the āhavanīya fire.

9.3.3.s: jīvann avabhṛthaṃ gachet /
9.3.3.d: जीवन्न् अवभृथं गछेत् /
9.3.3.m: If still living, he should go to the purificatory bath.
